title: He made the sky, the dark and the light. Yet.
subtitle: Praise first, then the strange choice to equate
then: This surah came down in Makkah in one sitting, late in the Prophet's ﷺ time there, when pressure on the believers was at its worst. It opens with praise for the One who made the heavens, the earth, the night and the day. Ibn Kathir notes the darkness is plural and the light singular: {idea}many ways to get lost, one way to see.{/idea} Then comes the sad word: {trap}yet they equate others with Him.{/trap}
now: You wake up, the light comes through the curtain, and before you have thanked anyone you have checked your phone, your bank app, your messages. Your mood for the day is already set by them. {trap}The things that steal your attention quietly take the seat of the One who made the morning.{/trap} {idea}Praise is just noticing who actually did it.{/idea}
old: Night and day just happen. Nothing to think about.
new: The light I wake up to was made, and the Maker deserves the first thought.
try: Tomorrow, when you first see daylight, say Alhamdulillah before you touch your phone.

title: Made from clay, given a deadline, and still in doubt.
subtitle: Two terms set by Allah: your death and the Hour

row.title: you doubt
sub: that He can bring you back

then: Ibn Kathir explains the clay as Adam, from whom people spread east and west. The first term is a person's death; the second, {idea}a term with Allah{/idea}, is the Hour, which none but He knows. The Makkans who heard this {trap}still doubted the return.{/trap}
now: You plan the next five years in a spreadsheet. Car loan, mortgage, the kids' school. One line is missing: the date that is already written. {trap}You argue about whether there is a next life, while you cannot say if you will see next month.{/trap} {idea}The One who started you from clay can finish the story.{/idea}
old: I have plenty of time. The end is far away.
new: My term is already set with Him. Doubt does not move the date.
try: Write one thing you would fix if you knew your term was this year. Do it this week.

title: He knows the hidden you and the public you.
subtitle: The same God everywhere, seeing both sides
then: Ibn Kathir explains: He is the One called Allah in the heavens and on the earth, worshipped by those above and below, {idea}who knows all affairs, public and secret.{/idea} For the Makkans who prayed to idols in public and kept their doubts in private, {trap}there was no hidden room.{/trap}
now: You are polite in the office meeting and something else in the car on the way home. One profile picture for the family, another tone in the anonymous comment section. {trap}You manage two audiences.{/trap} {idea}He is one audience who sees both, and is still the One you can turn to.{/idea}
old: What I do alone is my business. No one will know.
new: My secret and my public life are one open page to Allah.
try: Pick one thing you only do when no one is watching. Do the better version today, alone.

title: Every sign arrived, and every time they looked away.
subtitle: The habit of turning away from proof

row.title: turning away
sub: no proof lands on a back

then: Ibn Kathir says the stubborn idolaters of Makkah {trap}turned away from every sign, miracle and proof{/trap} of Allah's oneness and the truth of His messengers. They would not think about them or care about them. The issue was {idea}not a lack of signs but a lack of looking.{/idea}
now: A friend sends you a reminder video. You scroll past before it loads. A sermon starts at the wedding and you step outside to check your phone. A health scare makes you think for a day, then the thought is gone. {trap}Not refusing, just never facing it.{/trap} {idea}A sign only works on a face that turns toward it.{/idea}
old: If something real came to me, I would notice it.
new: Signs come all the time. The question is whether I turn toward them.
try: Next reminder you get today, a verse, a death notice, a kind word, stop and give it one full minute.

title: What they laughed at will come back as news.
subtitle: Mockery now, the report of it later
then: Ibn Kathir calls this a {trap}stern warning{/trap}: those who rejected the truth when it reached them would surely come to know the reality of what they used to deny. The Makkans were mocking the warning itself. {idea}The verse says: the joke will turn into news.{/idea}
now: The meme about the Day of Judgment in the group chat. The eye-roll when someone says "fear Allah." The laugh you join so you do not look old-fashioned. {trap}Mocking feels safe because nothing happens right away.{/trap} {idea}Delay is not denial of the news.{/idea}
old: It is only a joke. Nobody gets hurt.
new: What I laugh at today, I will meet as plain fact.
try: The next time a joke about faith comes up, simply do not laugh along.

title: They had more rain, more rivers, more power. Gone.
subtitle: Past generations stronger than you, replaced
then: Ibn Kathir says the earlier nations had more wealth, children, buildings, provision and soldiers than Quraysh. {reward}Rain came often and springs were plentiful.{/reward} Yet they were destroyed for their sins and others were raised after them, {idea}so the new ones would be tested too.{/idea}
now: Your pay rise came through. The house is paid off. Life is green and the rain keeps coming. {trap}It is easy to read comfort as approval.{/trap} Walk past an old family house that is now empty, or a company that was once a giant. {idea}Plenty is the test, not the grade.{/idea}
old: Things are going well, so I must be doing fine.
new: Blessings are a test of what I do with them, not a stamp of approval.
try: Look at one blessing you have right now and ask: how am I using this for good?

title: Even a book they could touch would be called magic.
subtitle: When the heart has decided, proof cannot land
then: Ibn Kathir explains: even if they {idea}saw the book come down and held it in their hands{/idea}, the disbelievers would say it was clear magic. He links it to other verses where, even climbing through a gate in the sky, they would say {trap}our eyes are dazzled.{/trap}
now: You have made up your mind about a person. They apologise; you say they are faking it. They help; you say they want something. {trap}Every new fact gets fitted into the old story.{/trap} {idea}The verse is a mirror: am I asking for proof, or protecting a decision?{/idea}
old: If the evidence were strong enough, I would change my mind.
new: If my heart is closed, no evidence will be strong enough.
try: Pick one opinion you hold firmly and honestly ask: what would change my mind?

title: Asking for an angel is asking for the end.
subtitle: The demand that would close the door on them
then: The Makkans demanded an angel be sent down with the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Kathir explains that if angels came while they kept the same attitude, {trap}the punishment would follow at once{/trap}, and he cites: on the day they see the angels there is no good news for the guilty. {reward}The absence of the angel was their time to think.{/reward}
now: You tell yourself: if Allah gave me one clear sign, I would change. A dream, a voice, something unmistakable. {trap}By the time it is unmistakable, it is too late to choose.{/trap} {idea}The quiet years, when nothing forces you, are exactly the mercy.{/idea}
old: I will change when I get a clear sign.
new: The time before the clear sign is the gift. After it, choices close.
try: Make one change today that you were waiting for a sign to make.

title: An angel messenger would still have to look human.
subtitle: Why a human messenger is the mercy

row.title: a man
sub: so they could talk to him

then: Ibn Kathir explains that an angel sent to people would come {idea}in the shape of a man{/idea}, since Ibn 'Abbas said they could not look at an angel's light. {reward}It is a mercy that each kind gets a messenger from its own kind{/reward}, someone they can talk to and learn from. Their {trap}confusion was self-made.{/trap}
now: You dismiss advice because it comes from your plain cousin, or the imam who drives an old car, or a coworker you think is no better than you. {trap}You want wisdom wrapped in something impressive.{/trap} {idea}Often guidance arrives in someone who eats, sleeps and works like you.{/idea}
old: If it came from someone ordinary, it cannot be that important.
new: Guidance through a human is a mercy, because I can learn from someone like me.
try: Think of good advice you brushed off because of who said it. Revisit it today.

title: Messengers were mocked before. The mockery came home.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ against ridicule
then: Ibn Kathir says this verse {reward}comforted the Messenger ﷺ{/reward} as his people denied him, and promised him and the believers victory and a good end in this life and the next. {trap}Those who scoffed at earlier messengers were surrounded by the very thing they mocked.{/trap}
now: You start praying at work and a colleague makes a comment. Your family laughs when you stop going to the late-night parties. {trap}It stings, and you start to wonder if you are the strange one.{/trap} {idea}Being laughed at for doing right puts you in very good company.{/idea}
old: If people laugh at me for this, maybe I am wrong.
new: Ridicule for doing right is an old road, and it ends well.
try: Keep one good habit today even if someone teases you for it. Smile and carry on.

title: Go and look at how the deniers ended.
subtitle: Travel as a lesson, not just a trip
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say: travel and see. Ibn Kathir explains it as {idea}think about yourselves and the afflictions that struck earlier nations{/idea} who denied their messengers, {reward}while the messengers and believers were saved.{/reward} Quraysh passed old ruins on their trade routes.
now: You visit a castle in ruins on holiday, take the selfie, buy the fridge magnet. Or you scroll past a news story about a once-huge brand that collapsed. {trap}You saw it but did not look.{/trap} {idea}Every ruin has a question for the visitor: what will be left of me?{/idea}
old: Old ruins are history. They have nothing to do with me.
new: Every end I see is a lesson about my own end.
try: Next time you pass something old or abandoned, pause and ask what its people would tell you.

title: He wrote mercy on Himself.
subtitle: The Owner of everything chose mercy
then: Just after warnings, the verse turns: everything belongs to Allah, and {reward}He has written mercy on Himself.{/reward} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith in the Two Sahihs: when Allah created the creation He wrote with Him above the Throne, {reward}My mercy overcomes My anger.{/reward} He will gather all on the Day, and those who {trap}lose themselves{/trap} do not believe in it.
now: It is 2 a.m. and you are lying awake replaying the thing you did. You picture Allah as a strict boss with a file on you. {idea}The Owner of the whole universe chose to bind Himself to mercy.{/idea} That is not a loophole. It is the door.
old: Allah is mostly waiting to catch my mistakes.
new: The One who owns everything wrote mercy on Himself first.
try: Before sleep tonight, ask Allah for mercy by name: Ya Rahman, Ya Rahim.

title: Whatever rests in the night and the day is His.
subtitle: All under His care, all heard, all known
then: Ibn Kathir explains that all creatures in the heavens and earth are {idea}Allah's servants, under His authority, power and will.{/idea} He {reward}hears what His servants say and knows their actions and secrets.{/reward} Said to Makkans who thought their gods shared that care.
now: The night shift in the hospital, when the corridor is empty. Your child asleep in the next room. The street outside, the cat on the wall. {reward}All of it rests in His hands while you rest.{/reward} {idea}Nothing you whisper at night goes unheard.{/idea}
old: At night, when everyone sleeps, I am on my own.
new: Everything resting in the night is His, me included, and He hears me.
try: Tonight, before sleep, say one thing to Allah you have not told anyone.

title: Why take a protector other than the One who feeds?
subtitle: He feeds everyone and needs no one
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask: shall I take a guardian other than Allah, {idea}who feeds and is not fed?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says He sustains creation without needing it. He cites a hadith where, after a meal at an Ansari's home, the Prophet ﷺ praised {reward}Allah who feeds but is never fed.{/reward}
now: Payday is late and your stomach drops. You think about the manager, the client, the one connection who can sort it. {trap}Without noticing, they become your protector.{/trap} {idea}Every person feeding you is being fed too. Only One feeds and needs nothing.{/idea}
old: My job and my contacts are what keep me going.
new: They are channels. The One who feeds them and me is my protector.
try: After your next meal, say the short dua: praise to Allah who fed me and gave me drink.

title: Even the Prophet ﷺ said: I fear, if I disobey.
subtitle: Healthy fear of a mighty Day

picture.label: What he is told to say

then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say openly that {trap}he fears the punishment of a mighty Day if he disobeys his Lord.{/trap} Ibn Kathir connects it to the next verse: {reward}whoever is spared that Day has received Allah's mercy, and that is the clear success.{/reward}
now: You feel pretty good about yourself compared to people on the news. {trap}The comparison makes fear feel unnecessary.{/trap} Then you read that the best of people said "I fear." {idea}Fear here is not panic. It is the seatbelt that keeps you safe on the road home.{/idea}
old: Fear of the Day is for people worse than me.
new: If the Prophet ﷺ said I fear, a little fear keeps me honest and hopeful.
try: Name one small disobedience you have gotten used to. Drop it for just today.

title: Being spared that Day is the real win.
subtitle: Success measured by what you are saved from
then: Following the Prophet's ﷺ words "I fear a mighty Day", this verse says: {reward}whoever is spared it has been shown mercy, and that is the clear success.{/reward} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: whoever is moved away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has succeeded, {idea}success meaning profit with no loss.{/idea}
now: The year-end review. The trophy at sports day. The number of likes on the wedding photos. {trap}You keep many scoreboards, and they all reset.{/trap} {reward}One result never resets: being shown mercy on that Day.{/reward}
old: Winning means getting ahead of others here.
new: Winning means being spared on the Day by His mercy.
try: Write down what you would call a successful life. Add one line about the Hereafter.

title: Only He can lift the harm He lets touch you.
subtitle: Harm and good both come from one hand
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah alone brings benefit or harm, and {idea}none can resist what He decrees.{/idea} He cites the Prophet's ﷺ supplication from the Sahih: {reward}O Allah, none can withhold what You give, nor give what You withhold.{/reward} The Makkans looked to idols for both.
now: You are in the hospital corridor waiting for the scan result. Or refreshing your inbox for the visa decision. {trap}Your whole hope sits on one doctor, one officer, one email.{/trap} {idea}They are doors. The key is with Him.{/idea} Knock there first.
old: This problem will be solved by the right contact.
new: Only Allah removes harm. People are the means He may use.
try: Before you make the next call about your problem, make a short dua first.

title: Above His servants, wise, and aware of everything.
subtitle: Power joined with wisdom
then: Ibn Kathir explains that to Allah {idea}the necks are subservient and the tyrants humble{/idea}; all creatures are under His power. Yet He is also {reward}the All-Wise who places everything in its rightful place.{/reward} For believers crushed by Quraysh, the strong men around them were not the top of the ladder.
now: The landlord who will not fix the heating. The manager who decides your shifts. {trap}Someone above you holds power, and it feels final.{/trap} {idea}Every person who has power over you has Someone over them.{/idea} And His power is never random.
old: The people above me decide my life.
new: Allah is above everyone over me, and He acts with wisdom.
try: When someone with power over you frustrates you today, say quietly: Allah is above them.

title: Allah is witness, and the Quran warns whoever it reaches.
subtitle: Including you, reading this now
then: Quraysh demanded a witness. The Prophet ﷺ is told: {idea}Allah is witness between me and you{/idea}, and this Quran came to warn you {reward}and whomever it reaches.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says it warns all who hear of it. Asked to agree there are other gods, he says: I bear no such witness.
now: A verse pops up on your screen between two adverts. Someone forwards a recitation in the family chat. {idea}It has reached you.{/idea} {trap}It is easy to file it as old text for other people.{/trap} The verse says the address line has your name on it.
old: The Quran was addressed to people long ago.
new: If it has reached me, it is speaking to me.
try: Read one verse today as if it were a message sent to you personally.

title: They knew him like they knew their own children.
subtitle: Recognizing the truth is not the same as accepting it

row.title: if I knew, I would follow

then: Ibn Kathir says the People of the Book knew what the Prophet ﷺ brought {idea}as they knew their own children{/idea}, because earlier prophets had given good news about him, his traits, his homeland and his migration. Yet {trap}those who lost themselves would not believe.{/trap}
now: You know smoking is hurting you. You know you owe your mother a call. You know the late prayer is late. {trap}Knowing is not the problem.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks what you do with what you already recognize as true.{/idea}
old: If I really knew it was true, I would act on it.
new: I often already know. The gap is between knowing and doing.
try: Pick one thing you know is right but keep postponing. Take one step on it today.

title: No one wrongs more than one who lies about Allah.
subtitle: Inventing or denying, both fail

key.label: What counts as lying about Allah

then: Ibn Kathir says no one is more unjust than {trap}one who claims Allah sent him when He did not{/trap}, or one who denies Allah's proofs, signs and evidence. {idea}Neither will ever succeed.{/idea} The Makkans claimed their idol customs came from God.
now: "Allah wants me to be rich, so this deal is fine." "The religion says you have to obey me in everything." {trap}It is easy to dress up our own wishes as Allah's will.{/trap} {idea}Being careful about what you claim He said is a serious kind of honesty.{/idea}
old: I would never lie about Allah.
new: Every time I say Allah wants this, I should be sure it is Him, not me.
try: Today, before saying the religion says, pause and ask if you actually know that.

title: Where are the partners you used to claim?
subtitle: The question on the Day of gathering
then: Ibn Kathir says on the Day of Resurrection Allah will ask the idolaters about the idols and rivals they worshipped instead of Him: {trap}Where are your partners whom you used to claim?{/trap} He cites the same question in Surat Al-Qasas. {idea}What they leaned on simply will not show up.{/idea}
now: The thing you spend most of your thinking on: the career, the approval of a parent, the body in the mirror. {trap}It feels like it will carry you.{/trap} Picture standing before Allah and looking around for it. {idea}Whatever will not be there, should not be on the throne now.{/idea}
old: What I rely on now will still be there for me.
new: Only what I did for Allah will show up on that Day.
try: Name the thing you lean on most besides Allah. Put it back in its place with a dua.

title: Their only answer: we never did it.
subtitle: The last excuse is denial
then: Ibn Kathir says their {trap}fitnah{/trap} here means their argument. Facing what is placed before them, the only thing left to say is: {trap}by Allah, our Lord, we were not idolaters.{/trap} {idea}The excuses they lived by have nothing left to say.{/idea}
now: You get caught out at work and the first word out of your mouth is "I didn't." Your child does the same with the broken vase. {trap}Denial is a reflex.{/trap} {idea}The verse shows where that reflex ends up if it becomes a way of life. Owning it now is the mercy.{/idea}
old: If I am caught, I can always deny it.
new: Admitting now, to Allah, is better than denying then.
try: Admit one mistake today, to Allah in dua, or to the person it affected.

title: Look how they lie to themselves.
subtitle: The invented things vanish when needed
then: Ibn Kathir notes the lie here is {trap}against themselves.{/trap} He links it to another verse where they are asked about their partners and say: {idea}they have vanished from us; in fact we never invoked anything.{/idea} What they had invented could not stay with them.
now: "I'm not addicted, I can stop any time." "It's not gossip, I'm just worried about her." {trap}The lies we tell ourselves are the hardest to see.{/trap} {idea}They fall apart exactly when we need them to hold.{/idea}
old: I know when I am lying.
new: The most dangerous lies are the ones I tell myself.
try: Catch one excuse you say to yourself often. Write the honest version next to it.

title: They listened, but nothing went in.
subtitle: Hearing the Quran without hearing it
then: Ibn Kathir says some came to hear the Prophet ﷺ recite, {trap}but it did not benefit them{/trap}; their hearts were veiled and their ears heavy. They came to argue and called it {trap}tales of the ancients{/trap}, copied from older books. He cites: {idea}had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear.{/idea}
now: The Friday sermon is on, and you are mentally planning the weekend. The Quran plays in the car while you argue with the satnav. {trap}The sound reaches you, the meaning does not.{/trap} {idea}Ears hear. Hearts listen.{/idea}
old: I hear the Quran a lot, so it is working on me.
new: Hearing is not listening. I need to open my heart to it.
try: Next time you hear a verse today, stop what you are doing and ask what it means.

title: They kept others away and stayed away themselves.
subtitle: Blocking good hurts the blocker most
then: Ibn ʿAbbas said this means they {trap}hindered people from believing{/trap} in the Prophet ﷺ. Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah said the disbelievers of Quraysh avoided meeting him and discouraged others from coming. Ibn Kathir says {idea}they combined both evils and destroyed only themselves.{/idea}
now: Your friend wants to start praying and you joke that she has gone too religious. Your brother tries to quit something bad and you invite him out anyway. {trap}Discouraging someone from good feels harmless.{/trap} {idea}The verse says the damage comes back to you.{/idea}
old: I am not stopping anyone. I just do not join.
new: Holding others back from good is a harm to my own soul.
try: Encourage one person today in a good thing they are trying to do.

title: If only we could go back. We would believe.
subtitle: The wish that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir describes the deniers made to stand before the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. {trap}They wish to be sent back{/trap} to do good deeds, stop denying the signs, and be believers. The Makkans hearing this {reward}were still in the life they would one day wish to return to.{/reward}
now: You are, right now, in the place people will beg to come back to. {idea}A normal Tuesday, a working body, time to pray.{/idea} {reward}The wish "if only I could go back" can be answered today, by living as if you already went back.{/reward}
old: There is time to sort myself out later.
new: I am living the chance others will wish they had.
try: Do one good deed today as if you had been sent back just to do it.

title: Sent back, they would do it all again.
subtitle: Fear of punishment is not change of heart
then: Ibn Kathir says what they used to hide in their hearts {trap}is uncovered{/trap}, and their wish to return is not real faith but {trap}fear of the torment in front of them.{/trap} He compares Pharaoh's people, who denied the signs though inwardly convinced. {idea}Returned, they would go back to the same.{/idea}
now: After the car accident you swear you will change. Two weeks later the habits are back. After the health scare, the same. {trap}Fear changes us for as long as we are afraid.{/trap} {idea}Ask Allah for the change that stays when the fear is gone.{/idea}
old: A big scare is what I need to change.
new: Change driven only by fear fades. A changed heart is what stays.
try: Think of a promise you made in a scary moment. Keep one part of it today.

title: This life is all there is, they said.
subtitle: The belief behind all the other choices
then: Ibn Kathir explains that even if returned, they would revert to saying: {trap}there is no life but this one, and we will not be raised.{/trap} This was the core belief of many in Makkah. {idea}Everything else they did grew from this root.{/idea}
now: "You only live once." On the gym wall, the holiday advert, the tattoo. {trap}It sounds like freedom.{/trap} But it quietly changes how you treat money, people and time. {idea}If there is a return, this life is the preparation, not the whole show.{/idea}
old: You only live once, so make the most of it.
new: I live once here, and it decides the life that follows.
try: Notice one choice today that you would make differently if you remembered the return.

title: Is this not the truth? Yes, by our Lord.
subtitle: The yes that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir explains they will stand before their Lord and be asked: {idea}is not the Resurrection true, unlike what you thought?{/idea} {trap}They will say: yes, by our Lord.{/trap} He links it to a verse asking: is this magic, or do you not see? {reward}The same yes today would have changed everything.{/reward}
now: Every day you get small chances to say yes. The prayer time alert. The urge to apologise. The verse you scroll past. {reward}A yes now is faith.{/reward} {trap}A yes when everything is visible is just seeing.{/trap}
old: I will believe properly when it is all clear.
new: Belief means saying yes now, before it is clear to the eye.
try: Say yes to one small call of conscience today without waiting to be sure.

title: The Hour comes suddenly, and the regret is heavy.
subtitle: Carrying your deeds on your own back
then: Ibn Kathir describes the regret of those who denied meeting Allah when {trap}the Hour comes on them all of a sudden{/trap}, and their sorrow for the good they never did. As-Suddi described a person's deeds meeting him in the grave and saying: {idea}in the world I carried you, today you carry me.{/idea}
now: You keep a list of things you will do "one day": make up the missed fasts, repay the cousin, read the whole Quran. {trap}The list assumes there will be warning.{/trap} {idea}The verse says the Hour does not book an appointment.{/idea} {reward}Every good deed you add is a lighter load.{/reward}
old: I will sort it out before the end. There will be signs.
new: The end can come suddenly, so I lighten my load today.
try: Take one item from your someday list and do it before tonight.

title: Most of this life is play. The next home is better.
subtitle: Keeping the game in its place
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {idea}most of worldly life is play and amusement{/idea}, while {reward}the home of the Hereafter is far better for those with taqwa.{/reward} The verse closes with a question to the Makkans, and to anyone: will you not use your mind?
now: Fantasy football, the new series, the sale on trainers. None of it is evil. {trap}The problem is when the game becomes the whole point.{/trap} {idea}Enjoy the play, but do not mistake it for the home you are going to.{/idea}
old: This life is the main event.
new: This life has play in it, but the real home is ahead.
try: Swap 15 minutes of scrolling today for something that builds your next home.

title: It is not you they reject. It is the truth.
subtitle: Allah sees the grief of the one who calls
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}We know your grief at what they say.{/reward} Ibn Kathir narrates that Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan and Al-Akhnas each secretly listened to his recitation at night. Abu Jahl later admitted: {trap}we competed with Banu Abd Manaf; how can we match a prophet? We will never believe.{/trap}
now: You share something true with your family and they shut you down. Your sister rolls her eyes when you mention prayer. {trap}It feels personal.{/trap} {idea}Often it is not about you at all; it is pride, rivalry or fear of change.{/idea} {reward}Allah sees the grief.{/reward}
old: When they reject what I say, they are rejecting me.
new: When people reject the truth, it is often their pride, not my failure.
try: Think of someone who rejected good advice from you. Make dua for them instead of resenting them.

title: They were denied and hurt, stayed patient, and help came.
subtitle: The pattern no one can change
then: Ibn Kathir says this {reward}comforted the Prophet ﷺ{/reward} and commanded him to be patient as the mighty messengers before him were. {idea}None can alter the Words of Allah{/idea}: His decision that victory, here and in the Hereafter, belongs to His believing servants.
now: You are doing the right thing at work, refusing the shortcut, and getting passed over for it. Months go by. {trap}It feels like the story ends here.{/trap} {idea}Every messenger had a middle chapter like this.{/idea} {reward}The help came after the patience, not instead of it.{/reward}
old: If doing right is this hard, maybe it is not worth it.
new: Hardship and patience come before help. That order is Allah's word.
try: Write down one hard thing you are holding steady on. Ask Allah for patience in it.

title: Dig a tunnel or climb to the sky, if you can.
subtitle: You cannot force anyone's heart
then: The Prophet ﷺ was {reward}eager for all people to believe{/reward}, Ibn ʿAbbas said. If their turning away was hard on him, then let him find a tunnel or a ladder and bring a better sign, if he could. {idea}Had Allah willed, He could have gathered them all on guidance.{/idea}
now: Your father will not listen. Your best friend keeps drifting. You send article after article, argue late into the night. {trap}You start to feel their guidance rests on you.{/trap} {idea}Your part is the message and the kindness. The heart belongs to Allah.{/idea}
old: If I just find the right argument, they will change.
new: I deliver with care. Allah opens hearts, not my effort.
try: Stop arguing with one person you are trying to change. Make dua for them tonight instead.

title: Only those who truly hear will answer.
subtitle: Living hearts respond; dead ones wait
then: Ibn Kathir says only {reward}those who hear, comprehend and understand{/reward} will accept the call. The "dead" here are those whose {trap}hearts are dead{/trap}; Allah will raise them and they will return to Him. He cites: a warning for whoever is alive.
now: Two people hear the same talk at the mosque. One goes home and calls his estranged brother. The other goes home and orders a takeaway. {idea}Same words, different hearts.{/idea} {reward}Keeping your heart alive is a daily thing.{/reward}
old: As long as I hear the reminders, I am fine.
new: The question is whether my heart is alive enough to respond.
try: Act on the last reminder you heard, even in a tiny way, today.

title: Allah can send a sign. The delay is wisdom.
subtitle: Miracles on demand carry a cost
then: The idolaters demanded a miracle of their choosing, like a spring gushing from the ground. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah is able{/idea}, but out of wisdom delayed it, because if He sent the sign they asked for and they still disbelieved, {trap}their punishment would come faster{/trap}, as with Thamud and the she-camel.
now: "If Allah just fixed this one thing, I would pray five times a day." You make deals in your head. {trap}You are setting the terms.{/trap} {reward}Sometimes the answer that does not come yet is the mercy, giving you room to come back on your own.{/reward}
old: If Allah gave me the sign I want, I would believe more.
new: Allah can give any sign. Holding it back can be His mercy to me.
try: Drop one if-then deal you have made with Allah. Just do the good thing anyway.

title: Every animal and bird is a community like you.
subtitle: Nothing is left out of His record
then: Qatadah said birds are a community, humans are a community, jinn are a community. Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah never forgets any creature, its provision or its affairs.{/reward} Abu Hurayrah said all creatures will be gathered, and {idea}justice will be so perfect that the hornless sheep is repaid by the horned one.{/idea}
now: The pigeons on your balcony. The stray cat you shoo away. The ants on the kitchen counter. {idea}Each is a community, known by name to Allah, fed by Him.{/idea} {trap}If He keeps their account, how you treat them is in the record too.{/trap}
old: Animals are just there. How I treat them does not matter.
new: Every creature is a community known to Allah, and how I treat it counts.
try: Put out water for a bird or animal today, or treat one gently on purpose.

title: Deaf, mute, and in layers of darkness.
subtitle: Rejecting the signs shuts down the senses
then: Ibn Kathir says those who reject the signs are {trap}like a deaf-mute person in darkness{/trap}: unable to hear, speak or see, how can they find the path? He links it to darkness upon darkness in a deep sea. {idea}Allah guides whom He wills onto a straight path.{/idea}
now: You have been ignoring your conscience for a while. Slowly the reminders stop reaching you. You do not feel bad anymore, you just feel nothing. {trap}That numbness is the darkness.{/trap} {reward}The way out is asking the One who gives light.{/reward}
old: I can always find my way back whenever I want.
new: Guidance is a light from Allah. I ask for it, I do not assume it.
try: Say "Ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim" slowly in your next prayer, and mean it.

title: When disaster hits, who would you call?
subtitle: The honest question of crisis
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask the idolaters: if punishment or the Hour came upon you, {idea}would you call on anyone other than Allah?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they would not, {trap}because they know none but He can remove the affliction.{/trap}
now: Turbulence on the plane. The phone call at 3 a.m. Your child's fever won't come down. {idea}In those seconds, no one thinks of their bank balance or their boss. You call Allah.{/idea} {trap}The verse asks why He is only the emergency number.{/trap}
old: I turn to Allah when things get really bad.
new: If He is the One I call in a crisis, He should be the One I call every day.
try: Make a dua today when nothing is wrong, just to thank Him.

title: In the storm, you forget your other gods.
subtitle: Necessity strips away the substitutes
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}in times of necessity you only call on Allah{/idea} and forget your idols and false deities. He links it to the verse about harm at sea, when {trap}those you call on besides Him vanish{/trap}, all except Him.
now: The lucky charm in your car, the horoscope app, the faith in "good vibes." On an ordinary day they feel useful. {trap}In a real emergency, you do not even remember them.{/trap} {idea}That moment shows you who you actually believe in.{/idea}
old: A little extra luck on the side doesn't hurt.
new: What I forget in a crisis was never real help.
try: Remove one small superstition or charm from your daily routine.

title: Hardship came so they might humble themselves.
subtitle: Poverty and illness as a call back
then: Allah sent messengers to many nations before. Ibn Kathir says He seized them with {trap}loss of wealth and diminished provision{/trap}, and with {trap}illness and pain{/trap}, {idea}so they might call on Allah with humility.{/idea}
now: Your hours get cut. The diagnosis comes back. The car breaks down the same week as the rent. {trap}It is easy to feel punished and abandoned.{/trap} {idea}The verse offers another reading: maybe this is an invitation to kneel and ask.{/idea}
old: Hard times mean Allah has turned away from me.
new: Hardship can be a call to come back to Him humbly.
try: In your next hard moment, make sujood and tell Allah exactly what is hurting.

title: The hardship came, but their hearts only hardened.
subtitle: When pain does not soften
then: Ibn Kathir explains: why did they not humble themselves when tested with disaster? {trap}Because their hearts were not soft or humble{/trap}, and Shaytan made their shirk, defiance and rebellion {trap}look attractive to them.{/trap}
now: Something bad happens and you get angry. At your parents, at the world, at Allah. You double down on the habit that caused it. {trap}Shaytan whispers that you deserve it.{/trap} {idea}The same pain can harden or soften you. You get to choose which.{/idea}
old: After all this, I have earned the right to be bitter.
new: Pain is meant to soften me. Bitterness is the trap.
try: Notice one area where hardship made you bitter. Say one sincere sentence of humility to Allah about it.

title: When they forgot, every door opened. Then the seizing.
subtitle: Ease after forgetting can be a warning
then: Ibn Kathir says after they ignored the warning, Allah {reward}opened the gates of provision{/reward} for them, and while they rejoiced, {trap}took them suddenly.{/trap} Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: whoever is given provision and thinks Allah is not testing him has no wisdom; and whoever has little and thinks Allah will not look at him has no wisdom.
now: You stopped praying a while ago and life got better. Promotion, new car, better holiday. {trap}You quietly conclude it did not matter.{/trap} {idea}Ease is not proof that forgetting is fine.{/idea} {reward}The doors are open; use them to walk back.{/reward}
old: Life is going great, so my choices must be fine.
new: Plenty after forgetting is a test, and a reason to remember.
try: Thank Allah out loud for one big blessing today, and use part of it for good.

title: The wrongdoers were cut off. All praise to Allah.
subtitle: Why justice ends in praise
then: After describing nations who forgot, enjoyed and were seized, the passage ends: {trap}the roots of the wrongdoing people were cut off{/trap}, {idea}and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.{/idea} For believers being persecuted in Makkah, this was a promise that wrong does not have the last word.
now: You read about a cheat who got away with it for years, a bully who never paid. It eats at you. {trap}It feels like wrong always wins.{/trap} {idea}The verse ends with praise because Allah's justice closes every account.{/idea} {reward}Your job is to stay on the right side of it.{/reward}
old: People who do wrong usually get away with it.
new: Wrongdoing gets cut off in the end, and Allah is praised for that justice.
try: Let go of one grudge about someone who wronged you. Leave the account with Allah.

title: If He took your hearing and sight, who would return them?
subtitle: Senses on loan from the One who gave them
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask: if Allah took your hearing and sight and sealed your hearts, {idea}who besides Him could give them back?{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes it may also mean losing the benefit of these senses in faith. Allah explains the signs in many ways, {trap}yet they turn aside.{/trap}
now: Your grandmother's eyesight fading. The friend with the sudden hearing loss. You squint at your phone at midnight without a thought. {reward}Every sound and colour today is a gift on loan.{/reward} {idea}And a heart that still understands is the biggest gift of the three.{/idea}
old: My senses are just how my body works.
new: My hearing, sight and heart are gifts Allah can take or keep.
try: Close your eyes for one minute today, then open them and thank Allah for sight.

title: Sudden or open, it falls only on the wrongdoers.
subtitle: Safety belongs to those who do not wrong
then: Ibn Kathir explains "suddenly" as while unaware or at night, and "openly" as by day. {trap}It strikes only those who wrong themselves by associating others with Allah{/trap}, while {reward}those who worship Him alone are saved, with no fear or sorrow.{/reward}
now: You read about earthquakes and pandemics and feel helpless. {trap}You cannot control when hard things come.{/trap} {idea}The verse shifts the question from when to who: what you can control is whether you are among the wrongdoers.{/idea}
old: Disaster is random. Nothing I do changes anything.
new: I cannot choose the timing, but I can choose not to be a wrongdoer.
try: Undo one small wrong today: return something, pay something, or say sorry.

title: Believe and set things right: no fear, no grief.
subtitle: The two-part job of every messenger
then: Ibn Kathir says messengers brought {reward}good news{/reward} and {trap}warnings{/trap}. Whoever believes in his heart and makes his deeds right by following them, {reward}has no fear about the future and no grief for what he left behind{/reward}, for Allah will look after what they leave.
now: You worry about your kids' future if something happens to you. You grieve the years you wasted before you got serious. {idea}The verse speaks to both: believe, and keep fixing what you can.{/idea} {reward}Allah takes care of the rest.{/reward}
old: I will always worry about the future and regret the past.
new: Faith with good deeds lifts both fear of the future and grief over the past.
try: Write one worry about your family's future. Hand it to Allah in dua tonight.

title: Denying the signs means meeting the cost of defiance.
subtitle: Consequences come from crossing limits
then: Right after the good news comes the warning. Ibn Kathir says the punishment touches them {trap}because they disbelieved in the messengers, defied Allah's commands, did what He forbade and crossed His limits.{/trap} {idea}It is the result of choices, not chance.{/idea}
now: Every time you push a limit, the excuse is ready: it's only small, everyone does it. {trap}Defiance is rarely one big moment. It is a habit of small crossings.{/trap} {idea}The verse links outcomes to those small steps.{/idea}
old: One small rule broken here and there does not matter.
new: Small, repeated defiance is what builds into real consequence.
try: Pick one limit you keep stepping over. Stay on the right side of it today.

title: No treasures, no unseen, no angel. Just the revelation.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ sets honest expectations
then: The Makkans wanted a prophet with riches, secret knowledge or angelic form. He is told to say: {idea}I am only a human to whom Allah sends revelation{/idea}, honoured with this duty. Ibn Kathir says he only knows of the unseen what Allah conveys. {trap}Are the blind and the seeing equal?{/trap}
now: The online guru who promises he knows your future. The healer who claims special powers for a fee. {trap}We are drawn to people who claim more than they should.{/trap} {idea}The best of creation claimed only to follow what was revealed.{/idea} That honesty is the test for anyone who teaches you.
old: A real religious guide should have special powers.
new: The truest guide claims nothing but following the revelation.
try: If you follow anyone online for religious advice, check today whether they claim more than they should.

title: Warn those who fear standing before their Lord.
subtitle: No protector or intercessor but Him
then: Ibn Kathir says warn with the Quran {idea}those who live in awe of their Lord{/idea}, who know that on that Day {trap}no relative or intercessor can prevent what He decides{/trap}. The aim is taqwa: {reward}that they work good deeds now, so those deeds save them then.{/reward}
now: You assume your parents' prayers, your family name, or the sheikh you follow will carry you through. {trap}On that Day, each stands alone before Allah.{/trap} {idea}The warning is not to scare you still; it is to get you moving today.{/idea}
old: Someone close to me will speak up for me.
new: Before Allah, my own deeds speak. So I work on them now.
try: Do one good deed today that is only yours, not your family's or community's.

title: Do not push away those who call on Allah morning and evening.
subtitle: The humble worshipper is your company

row.title: drop them to win the elite

then: Ibn Kathir says: do not turn away people with these qualities; {reward}make them your companions.{/reward} He compares Nuh, whose people mocked his lowly followers, and who answered: {idea}their account is only with my Lord.{/idea} Turning them away {trap}would itself be wrongdoing.{/trap}
now: The quiet uncle who always prays at the back. The cleaner who never misses Fajr at the mosque. {trap}At the event, you drift toward the people with influence.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks you to stay near the ones who call on Allah, whatever their status.{/idea}
old: I should spend my time with people who can help me get ahead.
new: The best company is those who call on Allah sincerely, whatever their status.
try: Sit with or greet someone at the mosque or work you usually overlook.

title: These poor people? Allah chose them over us?
subtitle: Status as a test of the proud
then: Ibn Kathir says most early followers were the weak: men, women, slaves, and few chiefs. Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan who followed the Prophet ﷺ, and was told the weak; Heraclius said such is the case with followers of messengers. {trap}Quraysh mocked and even tortured them{/trap}, saying, if it were good, these would not have reached it first.
now: The new convert from a poor background who knows more surahs than you. The young cousin who started praying before the adults. {trap}A small voice says: who are they to be ahead of me?{/trap} {idea}Allah knows best who is grateful, and gives guidance by that, not by rank.{/idea}
old: If something were really good, people like me would get it first.
new: Allah favors the grateful, and they often come from where I least expect.
try: Learn one thing today from someone you consider beneath you in status.

title: Greet them with peace. Your Lord wrote mercy on Himself.
subtitle: Wrong done in ignorance, then repentance
then: Right after the elite mocked the poor believers, the Prophet ﷺ is told to greet those same believers: {reward}peace be upon you.{/reward} Their Lord {reward}has written mercy on Himself{/reward}: whoever does wrong in ignorance, {idea}then repents and sets things right, will find Him Forgiving and Merciful.{/idea}
now: You walk into the mosque after years away, sure everyone is judging you. Or you messed up badly last week and cannot face your own prayer mat. {reward}The first word Allah tells His Prophet ﷺ to say to people like you is peace.{/reward} {idea}Then: repent, repair, and find mercy waiting.{/idea}
old: After what I did, I do not deserve a warm welcome.
new: Allah's welcome starts with peace, and repentance opens His mercy.
try: Greet someone with salam today who might feel unwelcome, or say it to yourself after a sincere tawbah.

title: Verses explained so the wrong path becomes obvious.
subtitle: Clarity shows both roads
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah explains {idea}whatever responsible adults need in life and religion{/idea}, so that {trap}the path of those who defy the prophets becomes clear.{/trap} He notes it may also mean: so that you, O Muhammad ﷺ, know the path of the criminals.
now: "Everyone has their own truth." "It's complicated." Sometimes it is. {trap}But often we blur things to avoid a choice.{/trap} {idea}The Quran's detail is there so you can see clearly which road is which.{/idea}
old: Right and wrong are too complicated to say.
new: Allah made the paths clear enough to choose.
try: Think of one grey area you hide behind. Look up what the Quran actually says about it.

title: I will not follow your desires and get lost.
subtitle: Saying no to the crowd's wishes
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to tell Quraysh plainly: {idea}I am forbidden to worship what you invoke besides Allah.{/idea} {trap}If I followed your desires, I would go astray{/trap} and not be among the guided. It was a refusal to compromise under heavy pressure.
now: The team wants you to fudge the numbers "just this quarter." Your friends push you to come along to something you know is wrong. {trap}Going along feels easier.{/trap} {idea}Following other people's desires is how a person quietly loses the way.{/idea}
old: Going along with everyone is the easier, safer choice.
new: Following others' desires against the truth is how I get lost.
try: Say a polite, clear no to one thing today you would normally go along with.

title: I stand on clear proof. The decision is Allah's.
subtitle: When they demanded the punishment now
then: Quraysh dared the Prophet ﷺ to bring the punishment. He is told to say: {idea}I am on clear proof from my Lord{/idea}, but {trap}I do not hold what you are rushing for.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says the ruling is with Allah: {reward}if He wills He punishes soon, if He wills He gives respite, out of His wisdom.{/reward}
now: In an argument, someone says: "If you're so right, why hasn't anything happened?" {trap}You feel pressure to prove your case on their timeline.{/trap} {idea}You can stand on what you know is true and leave the outcome with Allah.{/idea}
old: If I am right, I need to prove it now.
new: I can stand on the truth and leave the timing to Allah.
try: In your next disagreement, state your view calmly once, and do not chase the last word.

title: If it were in my hands, it would be settled already.
subtitle: Mercy chose patience instead
then: Ibn Kathir cites ʿA'ishah's hadith: after a painful rejection, the Angel of the Mountains offered to let two mountains close in on the Makkans. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ said no, hoping Allah would bring from them people who worship Him alone.{/reward} The verse states that the matter is {idea}not in his hands, but Allah's, who knows best the wrongdoers.{/idea}
now: Someone humiliates you, and for once you have the power to hit back: the screenshot, the complaint, the word to the boss. {trap}Settling it now feels like justice.{/trap} {reward}The Prophet ﷺ had real power to settle it and chose hope.{/reward}
old: If I could get back at them, I would.
new: Holding back when I could strike can be the bigger, more hopeful choice.
try: Think of someone who hurt you. Make dua for their good instead of their downfall.

title: Not a leaf falls without His knowing.
subtitle: The keys of the unseen are with Him alone

row.title: in a clear record
sub: fresh or dry, all of it

then: Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ in Al-Bukhari: {idea}the keys of the unseen are five, and none knows them but Allah{/idea}: the Hour, the rain, what is in the wombs, what a soul will earn tomorrow, and where it will die. His knowledge covers {reward}even the movement of a falling leaf{/reward}, so how much more the people He addresses.
now: You are walking to the bus stop in autumn, leaves coming down all around you. {idea}Each one is known.{/idea} So is the worry you have not told anyone, the job interview result you are waiting for, the small kindness nobody saw. {reward}Nothing about you falls unnoticed.{/reward}
old: Some things in my life are too small for Allah to notice.
new: If He knows every falling leaf, He knows every detail of me.
try: Next time you see a leaf fall, say SubhanAllah and remember one worry He already knows.

title: Every night He takes your soul. Every morning He returns it.
subtitle: Sleep as a small death, waking as a gift
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}sleep is the minor death{/idea}, and cites the verse where Allah takes souls at death and in sleep, keeping some and sending others back for a set term. He knows what you did by day, wakes you {reward}so your term may be completed{/reward}, then all return to Him.
now: Your alarm goes off and you groan. You reach for the phone. {reward}But a few seconds earlier your soul came back to you.{/reward} {idea}Not everyone who slept last night woke up.{/idea} The day ahead is extra time on a term that is still running.
old: Waking up is just what happens every morning.
new: Every morning, my soul was handed back to me for a reason.
try: Tomorrow, before checking your phone, say Alhamdulillah for being given your soul back.

title: Guardians sent over you, until the messengers come.
subtitle: Watched over in life, collected at death
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah sends {reward}angels who guard each person{/reward} and record their deeds, one on the right and one on the left. When one's lifespan ends, {idea}angels assigned to the task take the soul{/idea}, and {idea}they never neglect their duty.{/idea}
now: You cross the busy road without looking up from your screen and make it across. The car swerves just in time. {reward}Guardians you will never see were on shift.{/reward} {idea}The same angels are writing what you type in the next message.{/idea}
old: I am on my own out there.
new: I am guarded and recorded every moment, by Allah's order.
try: Before you post or send something today, remember the one on your right is writing too.

title: Returned to Allah, their true Master.
subtitle: The swiftest of those who take account

row.title: a Lord not angry
sub: the welcome for the good soul

then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith in Ahmad: angels attend the dying, and to a righteous soul they say, {reward}come out with honour, and receive good news of rest, satisfaction and a Lord who is not angry.{/reward} {idea}All souls are returned to their true Master{/idea}, whose judgment is His alone.
now: You sit in a hospital family room, waiting while someone you love slips away. {idea}They are going back to their Master.{/idea} {reward}The hope is to be welcomed by a Lord who is not angry.{/reward} That hope is shaped by today, not the last day.
old: Death is the end of the story.
new: Death is a return to my true Master, and I can prepare for the welcome.
try: Do one quiet deed today that you would like to be returned to Allah with.

title: In the dark storm you promise: save us, we will be grateful.
subtitle: The promises made in danger
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah saves His servants in times of need, {trap}in the darkness of land and sea, when storms strike{/trap}. Then {idea}they call on Him alone, without partners{/idea}. He links it to the verse of the ship caught by a storm, where the passengers cry: {reward}if You save us, we will truly be grateful.{/reward}
now: Turbulence over the ocean, the seatbelt sign pinging. A dark motorway with a flat tyre at 2 a.m. {idea}You whisper: Ya Allah, get me through this and I will change.{/idea} {trap}The question is what you do after you land.{/trap}
old: Those desperate prayers were just panic.
new: That cry was me knowing who really saves. I should keep the promise.
try: Remember a promise you made to Allah in a scary moment. Keep one piece of it today.

title: He saves you from every distress, then you forget.
subtitle: Comfort is where the partners come back
then: Allah answers the question of the storm: {reward}it is Allah who rescues you from it and from every distress.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says, {trap}yet you call on other gods in times of comfort.{/trap} He cites the verse: when He brings you safe to land, you turn away, and people are ever ungrateful.
now: The test result came back clear. The debt got paid off. The fight with your spouse got sorted. {trap}A week later, your prayer is rushed again and your thanks has gone quiet.{/trap} {idea}The rescue was His. The gratitude should outlast the relief.{/idea}
old: Once the problem is gone, life goes back to normal.
new: After He rescues me, the thanks should stay longer than the fear did.
try: Name one distress Allah has removed for you this year. Thank Him for it by name tonight.

title: From above, from below, or from each other.
subtitle: Division as one of the hardest trials
then: Jabir said when this verse came, the Prophet ﷺ said {idea}I seek refuge in Your Face{/idea} at the punishment from above and below, and of the third said it was lighter. Sa'd reported that he asked his Lord three things for his Ummah and was given two, but {trap}not that they be spared the violence of one another.{/trap}
now: The family WhatsApp group that split over an inheritance. The mosque committee that stopped talking. The cousins who have not spoken in years. {trap}Some of the hardest trials are the ones we cause each other.{/trap} {idea}Mending those cracks is part of seeking refuge.{/idea}
old: The real dangers are out there, not among us.
new: Division among us is itself a trial the Prophet ﷺ feared for us.
try: Send one message today to someone you have fallen out with. Just salam.

title: Your people denied it. Say: I am not your guardian.
subtitle: Conveying, not controlling
then: His own people, Quraysh, {trap}denied the Quran{/trap} though it was the truth. He is told to say: {idea}I have not been appointed a guardian or watcher over you.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says: my duty is to convey, yours to hear and obey; he cites, whoever wills, let him believe.
now: You keep checking whether your brother prayed, pushing your adult kids, policing your friends' choices. {trap}It turns into control, and it pushes them away.{/trap} {idea}Your part is to share the truth well. You are not their guardian.{/idea}
old: If someone close to me goes wrong, it is my failure.
new: I convey with love. Their choices are between them and Allah.
try: Let go of policing one person today. Share one good thing kindly instead.

title: Every piece of news has its moment. You will know.
subtitle: Promises land, perhaps after a while
then: Ibn ʿAbbas and others said: {idea}for every news there is a reality; it will happen, perhaps after a while.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to verses like: for each matter there is a decree. He calls it {trap}a warning{/trap} and {reward}a promise{/reward} that will surely occur.
now: You read Allah's promise that hardship comes with ease, but the ease has not arrived. {trap}You start to wonder.{/trap} {idea}Every promise has a date with Him.{/idea} {reward}You will know, in time.{/reward}
old: If it has not happened yet, maybe it will not.
new: Allah's words each have their time, and I will see them come true.
try: Write down one promise of Allah you are waiting on. Read it again whenever you doubt.

title: When they mock the verses, get up and leave.
subtitle: Walking away from mockery of faith
then: Ibn Kathir says this command {idea}includes every member of the Ummah{/idea}: do not sit with those who deny and mock Allah's verses. If you forget and sit, leave once you remember; {reward}forgetfulness is forgiven.{/reward} He links it to the verse: otherwise {trap}you would be like them.{/trap}
now: Lunch break, and someone starts making fun of the Quran for a laugh. Everyone chuckles. {trap}You stay, half-smiling.{/trap} {idea}You do not need a debate. You can just stand up, take your tray and go.{/idea}
old: If I stay quiet, I am not part of it.
new: Staying in a room that mocks the verses is a choice. I can quietly leave.
try: The next time talk turns to mocking faith, change the subject or leave politely.

title: You do not carry their account. Only remind.
subtitle: Leaving can itself be a reminder
then: Ibn Kathir says when believers avoid such company, {reward}they are free of the others' sin.{/reward} The reason for leaving is {idea}that the mockers become aware of their error{/idea}, avoid it, and never repeat it.
now: You quietly walk out of the conversation. A colleague notices and asks you about it later. {idea}Your leaving said more than an argument would have.{/idea} {reward}You do not carry their choices, only the chance to remind gently.{/reward}
old: Walking away means I have given up on them.
new: Walking away can be the reminder that helps them change.
try: If someone asks why you left a conversation, answer kindly in one honest sentence.

title: Leave those who turn religion into a game.
subtitle: But keep reminding, before a soul is held
then: Ibn Kathir says leave such people, yet {idea}remind people with the Quran{/idea} and warn them. The word tubsal was explained as being {trap}held, exposed, or kept from all good{/trap} because of what one earned. He cites: every soul is held by what it earned, except those on the right; and {trap}no ransom will be accepted.{/trap}
now: Religion as a costume: the Ramadan selfie, the Eid outfit, then nothing until next year. {trap}It is easy to slip into that ourselves.{/trap} {idea}The verse turns the warning inward first: is my faith something I play at, or something I live?{/idea}
old: Faith is something I do on special occasions.
new: Faith is not a game. What I earn is what I will be held by.
try: Pick one religious act you only do for show. Do it once today with no one watching.

title: Lost in the desert while friends call: come back to us.
subtitle: Turning back after being guided

row.title: companions
sub: come back, we are on the path

then: As-Suddi said some idolaters told Muslims to follow them and leave the Prophet's ﷺ religion. The answer: {trap}shall we turn on our heels after Allah guided us?{/trap} He gave the parable of {trap}a man who lost the road{/trap} while {reward}his companions called him back{/reward}, and he would not come. {idea}Allah's guidance is the guidance.{/idea}
now: You used to pray. Then new friends, a new city, a new job, and slowly you drifted. {reward}Your old friend still texts: come to the halaqa on Thursday.{/reward} {trap}You keep saying next week.{/trap} {idea}The ones calling you back are a mercy. Answer them.{/idea}
old: I drifted a bit, but I can always find my own way back.
new: When I am drifting, the people calling me back are Allah's mercy.
try: Reply to the person who keeps inviting you to something good. Say yes once.

title: Pray, be mindful, and know you will be gathered to Him.
subtitle: What submission looks like day to day

row.title: submit
sub: to the Lord of the worlds

then: Continuing the answer to those who invited the Muslims back, Ibn Kathir says {idea}we were commanded to perform the prayer and to fear Allah in all circumstances{/idea}, {reward}and it is He to whom you will be gathered{/reward} on the Day of Resurrection.
now: You feel inspired after a talk, then Monday comes. {trap}Inspiration fades by lunch.{/trap} {idea}The verse turns guidance into something you can do: the next prayer on time, a mindful choice at work.{/idea} {reward}Those small steps keep you on the path.{/reward}
old: Feeling close to Allah is what keeps me guided.
new: Prayer and mindfulness, done daily, keep me on the path.
try: Set an alarm for the next prayer and pray it the moment it goes off.

title: He says Be, and it is. The Horn Day is His.
subtitle: Creation in truth, and a Day that comes in a blink
then: Ibn Kathir says He created the heavens and earth {idea}in justice{/idea}, and the Day of Resurrection will come {idea}faster than the blink of an eye{/idea} when He says Be. He cites the Prophet ﷺ in Muslim: {trap}Israfil has the Horn to his mouth and his forehead lowered, awaiting the command to blow.{/trap}
now: You plan a five-year career path, a ten-year mortgage. Elections come and go, empires on the news rise and fall. {trap}It all feels permanent.{/trap} {idea}One word from Allah, and every kingdom is His alone.{/idea} {reward}The only plan that lasts is the one made for that Day.{/reward}
old: The powers of this world will always be in charge.
new: All dominion returns to Allah the moment He says Be.
try: Next time the news makes you anxious, say: the kingdom belongs to Allah.

title: Ibrahim to his father: do you take idols as gods?
subtitle: Truth spoken to the closest person

row.title: honest and gentle
sub: peace be on you, I will pray for you

then: Ibrahim advised his father and forbade him from idol worship. Ibn Kathir cites Surah Maryam, where he speaks to him as {reward}"O my father"{/reward} again and again, and when threatened, replies: {reward}peace be on you, I will ask my Lord to forgive you.{/reward} He kept praying for him through his father's life.
now: Your dad has a habit you know is harming him. Your mum believes something you are sure is wrong. {trap}Saying nothing feels kinder, or saying it harshly feels braver.{/trap} {idea}Ibrahim did neither. He was clear, he was gentle, and he kept praying.{/idea}
old: Telling family hard truths only causes fights.
new: I can be clear with family and still speak with respect and pray for them.
try: Make dua tonight, by name, for a family member you disagree with.

title: Shown the kingdom of the heavens, to be certain.
subtitle: Looking at creation leads to conviction
then: Ibn Kathir says when Ibrahim {idea}contemplated the creation of the heavens and earth{/idea}, Allah showed him proofs of His oneness over His dominion. The aim: that he be {reward}among those with certain faith.{/reward} He links it to the command: behold all that is in the heavens and the earth.
now: You walk to the car under a clear night sky and never look up. You scroll past a photo of a galaxy in two seconds. {trap}Faith that is only inherited can feel thin.{/trap} {idea}Ibrahim's certainty grew by actually looking.{/idea}
old: My faith is just what I was raised with.
new: Reflecting on creation can turn inherited faith into certainty.
try: Go outside tonight and look at the sky for two full minutes without your phone.

title: The star set. I do not love what disappears.
subtitle: A lord cannot be something that fades
then: His people worshipped heavenly bodies. When night covered him, Ibrahim saw a star and said, this is my lord, and when it set, {idea}I do not love those that set.{/idea} Qatadah said: {reward}Ibrahim knew that his Lord is Eternal and never ceases.{/reward}
now: The new phone that is old in a year. The celebrity everyone loved last summer. The relationship that felt like everything. {trap}We give our hearts to things that set.{/trap} {idea}Love them as gifts, but save your worship for the One who never disappears.{/idea}
old: What shines brightest right now deserves my devotion.
new: Anything that sets cannot be my lord. Only the Eternal deserves that.
try: Name one thing that has your heart that will one day set. Thank Allah for it as a gift.

title: Unless my Lord guides me, I will be lost.
subtitle: The moon rose, set, and he asked for guidance
then: Next Ibrahim saw the moon rising and said, this is my lord. When it set, he did not only conclude; {idea}he turned to his real Lord{/idea}: {reward}unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people gone astray.{/reward}
now: You research everything: the best phone, the best school, the best diet. {trap}With faith too, you read and argue and reason, but forget to ask.{/trap} {idea}Ibrahim reasoned brilliantly and still said: guide me.{/idea}
old: If I think hard enough, I will figure out the truth on my own.
new: Even my best thinking needs Allah's guidance to land right.
try: Before reading or studying anything about faith today, ask Allah to guide you through it.

title: Even the sun set. I am free of your partners.
subtitle: The greatest thing he saw still was not God
then: Then Ibrahim saw the sun rising, {idea}bigger and more radiant than the star and moon{/idea}, and said: this is my lord, this is greater. {trap}When it too set{/trap}, he declared: {reward}O my people, I am free from what you associate with Allah.{/reward}
now: You picture the biggest thing you could rely on: a huge salary, a powerful family, a country's protection. {trap}Even the biggest of these sets one day.{/trap} {idea}Ibrahim tested the greatest thing he could see, and it still was not God.{/idea}
old: If something is big and powerful enough, I can rely on it.
new: Even the greatest created thing sets. Only Allah stays.
try: Watch the sunset today, or picture it, and say: I am free of every false lord.

title: I have turned my face to the Maker of the heavens.
subtitle: Sincerely, inclining to the truth
then: Ibrahim's conclusion: {idea}I have turned my face toward Him who created the heavens and the earth.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it means {reward}I have purified my religion and made my worship sincere{/reward} to the One who originated them without precedent, hanif, avoiding shirk and embracing tawhid.
now: You pray, but part of you is always also facing the boss's approval, the bank balance, what people think. {trap}Your face is split.{/trap} {idea}Turning your face is the decision to point everything in one direction, toward the Maker.{/idea}
old: I can face Allah and the world's approval at once.
new: Turning my face to Allah means making my worship sincerely His.
try: In your next prayer, say the opening dua of turning your face to the Creator, slowly.

title: You argue with me about Allah, when He guided me?
subtitle: No fear of false gods
then: His people argued and raised doubts. Ibrahim said: {idea}do you dispute with me about Allah when He has guided me?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says he told them their gods have no effect, so {reward}I do not fear them{/reward}; only Allah brings benefit or harm. He compares Prophet Hud saying: plot against me all of you.
now: Someone warns you about the evil eye, the unlucky number, the curse on the family. {trap}Fear creeps in.{/trap} {idea}Nothing reaches you unless Allah wills it, and His knowledge surrounds everything.{/idea}
old: Bad luck, curses or jinxes can get me if I am not careful.
new: Nothing harms me except what Allah wills. I fear Him, not them.
try: When a superstition worries you today, say: nothing happens except what my Lord wills.

title: Which side has more right to feel safe?
subtitle: Turning their fear back on them
then: Ibrahim asked: {trap}how should I fear your idols, when you do not fear{/trap} associating with Allah things for which He sent you no authority? Ibn ʿAbbas said authority here means proof. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}which party has more right to be safe from Allah's punishment on the Day?{/idea}
now: Your friends say you are taking a risk by quitting the shady side-business. "What if money dries up?" {trap}They fear the wrong thing.{/trap} {idea}The real risk is relying on what has no backing from Allah.{/idea}
old: Leaving what everyone relies on is the risky choice.
new: The real risk is relying on what Allah gave no authority to.
try: List one thing you fear losing if you do right. Ask: is that fear backed by any proof?

title: Faith not mixed with injustice brings safety and guidance.
subtitle: The Companions feared the verse, then were taught
then: When this came down, the Companions said: {trap}who among us has not wronged himself?{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said it is not what they understood, and pointed to Luqman's words: {idea}shirk is a great wrong.{/idea} So {reward}those who worship Allah alone have security on the Day, and are the guided.{/reward}
now: You read a strict verse and your heart sinks: I have made so many mistakes, there is no hope for me. {trap}You give up before you read the explanation.{/trap} {reward}The Companions felt the same, and the Prophet ﷺ gently showed them the meaning.{/reward} {idea}Ask before you despair.{/idea}
old: If I have done wrong, I have no right to feel safe with Allah.
new: Keeping my faith free of shirk is the heart of safety, and He forgives much.
try: Next time a verse frightens you, look up its explanation before drawing conclusions.

title: That was Our argument, given to Ibrahim.
subtitle: Allah raises in rank whom He wills
then: Mujahid and others said "Our proof" means Ibrahim's question: {idea}which of the two parties has more right to safety?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says Allah directed him to proclaim it, and Allah {reward}testified to his words{/reward} by confirming security and guidance for the sincere.
now: You finally find the right words in a hard conversation, words that calm a fight or make your point clear. {trap}It is tempting to feel clever.{/trap} {idea}Clarity is a gift from Allah, and He raises whom He wills.{/idea}
old: When I win an argument, it is because I am smart.
new: The right words come from Allah. My rank is in His hands.
try: After your next good conversation, say Alhamdulillah for the words He gave you.

title: He left his people, and was given a family of prophets.
subtitle: What Allah gives back to those who leave for Him
then: Ibn Kathir says when Ibrahim and Sarah had lost hope of children, Allah gave them Ishaq, and the good news of Ya'qub after him. {reward}This was a reward for Ibrahim, who left his people and land to worship Allah alone{/reward}; Allah gave him {reward}better than his tribe.{/reward} Nuh was guided before him too.
now: You stopped going out with the old crowd because of what they did. Weekends are lonely now. {trap}It feels like you lost a whole circle.{/trap} {reward}Ibrahim left a whole people and was given a family of prophets.{/reward} {idea}What you leave for Allah, He replaces with better.{/idea}
old: If I leave my circle for Allah, I will end up alone.
new: What I give up for Allah, He replaces with something better.
try: Ask Allah tonight for good company to replace what you left for His sake.

title: Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa and Ilyas: all among the righteous.
subtitle: A chain of righteous names
then: The list of guided prophets continues. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}mentioning Isa among the offspring of Ibrahim or Nuh shows a daughter's children count as a man's offspring{/idea}, since Isa had no father and is counted {reward}through his mother Maryam.{/reward} Each one, the verse says, was righteous.
now: You flip through the family photo album: grandparents, aunts, your mother's side you rarely visit. {idea}Allah counted Isa through his mother.{/idea} {reward}Every branch of your family is part of your story, and righteousness can run through any of them.{/reward}
old: Only one side of my family really counts.
new: Righteousness passes through every line, mothers' as much as fathers'.
try: Call a relative on your mother's side today and ask how they are.

title: Four very different lives, all raised above the worlds.
subtitle: Ismail, Al-Yasa, Yunus and Lut in one line

row.title: preferred
sub: above the people of their time

then: This verse closes a long list of prophets that began with Ibrahim. The Quraysh were pressing the Prophet ﷺ hard in Makkah. Allah names {idea}a whole family of guided people{/idea} who walked the same road before him, and says {reward}each one was preferred above the worlds{/reward}.
now: You scroll past people whose lives look nothing like yours. One stayed in a small town. One ran away and came back. One stood alone against a whole street. {idea}Allah lifted each of them, in a different shape of life.{/idea} Your shape counts too.
old: Only one kind of life is worth honoring, and mine is not it.
new: Allah raised people through very different stories. Mine can be one of them.
try: Read the names in 6:83-86 slowly today. Pick the one whose story you know least and look it up.

title: Guidance ran through fathers, children and brothers.
subtitle: A chosen family line, and a straight path

row.title: Allah chooses
sub: among them, not all of them

then: After naming the prophets, the verse widens to their families. Ibn Kathir notes how Allah placed {reward}prophethood and the Book in the offspring of Nuh and Ibrahim{/reward}. The word is {idea}some of{/idea} them: guidance ran through families, but each person was still chosen.
now: Your grandmother prayed every night. Your cousin memorized Quran. Your brother drifted away. Families carry faith, but {idea}nobody inherits it like a house.{/idea} You can be the link that carries it on, or the one who starts it.
old: My family is religious, so I am covered.
new: A family can carry guidance, but each of us still walks the path ourselves.
try: Ask one older relative how they came to pray. Listen without rushing.

title: Even prophets' deeds would vanish if mixed with shirk.
subtitle: Guidance is Allah's, and shirk cancels everything

row.title: guidance of Allah
sub: He gives it to whom He wills

then: The list of prophets is followed by a startling line. {idea}This is Allah's guidance, His to give.{/idea} And even these chosen men, if they had joined partners with Allah, {trap}all their work would have come to nothing.{/trap} The Quraysh heard it while they worshipped idols beside Allah.
now: You fast, you give, you help at the mosque. Then you catch yourself hoping people notice, or leaning on a charm, a person, a lucky number. {trap}The bricks are only as safe as the ground under them.{/trap} {idea}Keep the ground clean.{/idea}
old: As long as I do a lot of good, the details of who it is for do not matter.
new: Who my deeds are for decides whether they stand at all.
try: Before one good deed today, pause and say quietly: this is for You, Allah.

title: If these people refuse it, others will carry it.
subtitle: The message never depends on one crowd
then: The leaders of Makkah thought that without them the message would die. The verse answers calmly. {reward}Book, wisdom and prophethood{/reward} were given to these prophets. {idea}If these people deny it, Allah has already entrusted it to others{/idea} who will not deny it.
now: You drop the Quran class because work is busy. You tell yourself the group will fall apart. It does not. Someone else steps in. {idea}The work continues with or without you.{/idea} {reward}The honor of carrying it is what you miss.{/reward}
old: If I step back, the good work will collapse.
new: The work will go on. The question is whether I will be part of it.
try: Think of one good thing you quietly stopped doing. Do one small piece of it again this week.

title: Follow their guidance, and ask for nothing in return.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ told to take these men as models
then: After the long list of names, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}these are the ones Allah guided, so follow their guidance.{/idea} Then he is told to say he asks no payment. {reward}It is only a reminder for the worlds.{/reward} Makkah could not accuse him of selling it.
now: You want to grow, so you follow fifty accounts and a dozen gurus. Many of them are selling something. {idea}Here is a short list of people worth copying{/idea}, and the one who brought it asked you for nothing. Start with the ones who did not need your money.
old: I will pick my role models from whoever is loudest right now.
new: The best models are the ones Allah guided, and they asked nothing of me.
try: Pick one prophet from this list. Write down one habit of his you could copy this week.

title: They said Allah never speaks to humans. Then who sent Musa's book?
subtitle: Underestimating Allah, and picking pages from scripture
then: Ibn Abbas and others said this was about the Quraysh, and some said it was about some Jews. They claimed {trap}Allah sends nothing down to any human.{/trap} The reply: then who sent the book Musa brought, {idea}a light and guidance{/idea}, which some had split into pages, showing parts and hiding the rest.
now: You quote the verse that suits you in the argument and skip the one that does not. You screenshot half a hadith for the group chat. {trap}Showing some pages and hiding others{/trap} is easy with a phone. {idea}Take the whole book seriously, including the parts that pinch.{/idea}
old: I can keep the parts of revelation that fit me and quietly skip the rest.
new: Picking pages is a way of not valuing Allah as He deserves.
try: Find one verse you tend to avoid because it asks something of you. Read it with its tafsir today.
