title: A blessed Book, and those who believe it guard their prayer.
subtitle: The Quran sent to Makkah and everyone around it
then: Right after the Tawrah, Allah points to {reward}this blessed Book{/reward}, the Quran, sent to warn Makkah, the Mother of Towns, and those around it. Ibn Kathir says that means all people. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and {idea}they keep guarding their prayers.{/idea}
now: You say the Quran matters to you. Then the afternoon meeting runs long and Asr slips by again. {idea}Belief in the next life shows up in a calendar.{/idea} Guarding something means you plan around it, not fit it in.
old: My faith is in my heart, my schedule is a separate thing.
new: Believing in the Hereafter shows in how I protect my prayers.
try: Put the next prayer time in your phone calendar as a meeting you cannot move.

title: Nothing is more unjust than lying in Allah's name.
subtitle: False claims of revelation, and the moment of death
then: Ikrimah and Qatadah said part of this was about Musaylimah, who claimed revelation. Others boasted they could say something like the Quran. The verse calls this {trap}the greatest injustice{/trap}, then shows the moment of death, when the angels tell such people their humiliation comes {trap}for what they said against Allah{/trap} and their arrogance.
now: You hear someone say "Islam says..." about something they just made up. Maybe you have done it, to win an argument or sound sure. {idea}Words about Allah are not small talk.{/idea} It is fine to say "I do not know."
old: Saying what I think religion says is harmless, even if I am not sure.
new: Putting words in Allah's mouth is among the heaviest wrongs there is.
try: Next time you are unsure what Islam says on something, say I do not know, and look it up later.

title: You come back alone, the way you first came.
subtitle: Everything given is left behind on that Day
then: On the Day of Return it will be said: {idea}you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith where the son of Adam says "my money, my money," yet {reward}he only keeps what he ate, wore, or gave in charity.{/reward} The idols they relied on are nowhere.
now: Moving house, you see how much stuff you own. Boxes of it. Now picture leaving with nothing in your hands. {idea}No phone, no contacts, no one to vouch for you.{/idea} {reward}What you gave away is the only thing already packed.{/reward}
old: What I build up and who I know will carry me.
new: I arrive alone, and only what I sent ahead is waiting.
try: Give away one thing today you were keeping just to keep it.

title: He splits the seed and brings life out of dead things.
subtitle: Recognizing Allah in a sprouting grain
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah makes {idea}the lifeless seed and fruit stone split and sprout{/idea}, giving many kinds of plants. He brings life from what is dead and the dead from the living. {idea}That is Allah{/idea}, so how could the people of Makkah be turned away to worshipping others?
now: A chickpea left in a damp jar on the windowsill. Three days later, a tiny white root. You have seen it a hundred times and never stopped. {idea}Something dry and dead pushed out a living thing.{/idea} That is a signature.
old: Seeds sprouting is just science, nothing to think about.
new: Every sprout is Allah bringing life out of something dead, right in front of me.
try: Soak a few seeds or lentils in water tonight. Watch them over the next days and say SubhanAllah when they open.

title: He breaks the dawn and gives the night for rest.
subtitle: Day, night, sun and moon on exact measure

row.title: rest
sub: a gift built into the day

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is the Creator of light and darkness. {reward}He splits the darkness with dawn{/reward} and makes the night still so creatures can rest. The sun and moon run fixed courses that set seasons and the length of days. {idea}This is the measuring of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.{/idea}
now: It is 1 a.m. and you are still scrolling, telling yourself you will sleep soon. {reward}The night was made for rest, on purpose.{/reward} {trap}You keep fighting a gift.{/trap} Sunrise tomorrow will come on time, whether you are ready or not.
old: Night is just extra time I can use however I want.
new: Night is a gift of rest, measured out by the One who knows what I need.
try: Tonight put your phone in another room thirty minutes before you sleep.

title: Stars were placed to guide you through the dark.
subtitle: Signs laid out in detail for people who know
then: The Arabs crossed deserts and seas by night, steering by the stars. Allah says {idea}He placed them so you could find your way in the dark.{/idea} Ibn Kathir quotes some of the early scholars: stars are for {reward}beauty, guarding the sky, and direction{/reward}, and anyone who claims more has made a mistake.
now: Your phone shows your horoscope next to the weather. Half joking, you read it. {idea}The stars were made to guide your feet, not to run your future.{/idea} The same sky that guided caravans is still pointing to the One who set it there.
old: The stars might say something about my luck.
new: The stars are signs that guide, pointing me back to Allah who placed them.
try: Step outside tonight, find one star, and thank Allah for one way He guided you this year.

title: One soul for all of us, then a stay and a storage.
subtitle: One origin, and the places we pass through
then: Ibn Kathir says the single soul is Adam. The scholars explained the two words in different ways: {idea}a place of stay in the womb and a place of storage in the father's loins{/idea}, or this life and the grave after it. Either way, {idea}every person has stations they pass through.{/idea}
now: The cleaner at your office, the stranger on the bus, the cousin you avoid at weddings. {idea}Same first father.{/idea} And each of you is only passing through this station. The grave is the next stop for all of you.
old: People who are not like me are a different kind of human.
new: We all come from one soul and pass through the same stations.
try: Greet someone today you normally walk past without a word.

title: Look at the fruit as it forms and as it ripens.
subtitle: Rain, grain, dates, grapes, olives, pomegranates
then: Ibn Kathir notes dates and grapes were the most precious fruits to the people of the Hijaz. Allah describes them hanging low, easy to pick, with olives and pomegranates whose leaves look alike but whose fruit differs. Then a direct command: {idea}look at the fruit when it forms and when it ripens.{/idea} {reward}In this are signs for people who believe.{/reward}
now: You grab a pomegranate at the supermarket without looking. Same water, same soil, yet each fruit has its own color and taste. {idea}The verse literally tells you to look.{/idea} Slow down at the fruit stand once.
old: Fruit is just food. There is nothing to see in it.
new: Every fruit is a sign, if I actually stop and look at it.
try: Before you eat a piece of fruit today, look at it for ten seconds and think about where it came from.

title: They made partners of the jinn He created.
subtitle: Inventing sons and daughters for Allah without knowledge
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the idol worshippers {trap}obeyed the jinn who told them to worship idols{/trap}, so in effect they worshipped the jinn. They also invented children for Allah, like the pagan claim that angels were His daughters. The answer is short: {idea}He created them.{/idea} How can a creation share the Creator's place?
now: You would never call anything a god. But there is a voice you obey even when you know it is wrong. A craving, an influencer, the fear of what people say. {trap}Obeying it is a kind of worship.{/trap} {idea}It too is just something Allah created.{/idea}
old: Shirk is about statues, nothing to do with me.
new: Whatever I obey against Allah is taking a place only the Creator deserves.
try: Notice one voice today that pulls you against what you know is right. Name it, and say: Allah created you.

title: The One who made the heavens from nothing needs no son.
subtitle: Badi: the Originator with no model to copy

row.title: Badi
sub: made it all with no precedent

then: Mujahid and As-Suddi explained Badi as the One who {idea}brought the heavens and earth into being with no earlier example.{/idea} A child comes from two matching partners, Ibn Kathir notes, and {trap}nothing is like Allah{/trap} to be His partner. He created everything and knows everything.
now: We picture Allah the way we picture people: tired, needing help, needing someone to carry on His name. {idea}The One who made galaxies from nothing has no needs at all.{/idea} That is why you can bring Him every need of yours.
old: I quietly imagine Allah with human limits, like someone who might be too busy for me.
new: He made everything from nothing and needs nothing, so nothing I ask is too much.
try: Ask Allah today for something you thought was too big to ask for.

title: That is your Lord. He made everything, so worship Him.
subtitle: Creator of all, and the Guardian over all
then: After the proofs of seeds, dawn, stars and rain, the verse draws the conclusion. {idea}That is Allah, your Lord, Creator of all things, so worship Him.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains Wakil as {reward}the Trustee and Watcher who gives provision and protection by day and night.{/reward}
now: Three a.m. and you are lying awake, running through bills, your child's grades, your mother's test results. {trap}You act as if you are holding up the whole sky.{/trap} {reward}There is a Guardian over all things, and He does not sleep.{/reward}
old: If I stop worrying, everything will fall apart.
new: Allah is the Guardian over all things. My job is to worship Him and do my part.
try: Write down your top worry, then say Hasbiyallah wa nimal wakil over it.

title: No eye can grasp Him, yet He sees every eye.
subtitle: The Subtle, the Fully Aware
then: Aishah used this verse to show that no one sees Allah in this life. Ibn Kathir says it does not deny that believers will see Him in the Hereafter, but {idea}no vision can ever encompass Him.{/idea} He, though, {reward}encompasses all vision{/reward}, the Subtle who knows where every thing is.
now: You are alone in your room with your phone. No one can see your screen. {idea}You cannot see Him, but He sees exactly what you see.{/idea} That can feel heavy. It is also a comfort on the nights you cry where no one notices.
old: If no one can see me, it is like it did not happen.
new: He sees every glance and every quiet tear, even when I cannot see Him.
try: The next time you are alone with your phone, pause and remember He sees what you see.

title: The proofs have come. Seeing them is for your own good.
subtitle: Clear insight arrives, and each person chooses to look
then: Ibn Kathir explains Basa'ir as {idea}the proofs in the Quran and the message of the Prophet ﷺ.{/idea} Whoever sees gains for himself. Whoever turns blind {trap}harms only himself{/trap}, for it is the heart that goes blind, not the eyes. The Prophet ﷺ only conveys. He is not their keeper.
now: Your friend sends you a talk that could change how you see your anger. You leave it unopened for weeks. {idea}Nobody can force you to look.{/idea} {trap}Not looking is still a choice{/trap}, and you are the one who carries it.
old: If guidance really mattered, someone would make me listen.
new: The light is already here. Looking or not looking is mine to answer for.
try: Open one reminder you have been saving for later and actually read or watch it today.

title: Explained from every angle, and still they said he copied it.
subtitle: The same verses clarify for some and harden others
then: Allah explains His signs in many ways in this surah, mainly that none deserves worship but Him. Ibn Abbas and others said the deniers responded: {trap}you studied this with people of earlier scripture.{/trap} Yet the same explanations {reward}make things clear for people who know{/reward} and want the truth.
now: Two people hear the same khutbah. One leaves moved and changes something. The other says, "He just read that off some website." {idea}Same words, different hearts.{/idea} You get to pick which listener you are.
old: If something were really true, everyone would see it the same way.
new: Truth can be fully clear and still be refused. The heart decides how it lands.
try: Next time you feel like dismissing a reminder, ask yourself: am I looking for truth or an excuse?

title: Follow what was revealed, and turn away from the mockers.
subtitle: Stick to revelation, and stop chasing every insult
then: In the hardest years in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ is told: {idea}follow what has been revealed to you{/idea}, and turn aside from those who join partners with Allah. Ibn Kathir explains turning aside as {reward}forgiving them, being patient, and enduring their harm{/reward} until Allah brings relief and support.
now: Someone at work mocks your prayer breaks. A cousin keeps sending sarcastic memes. You draft long replies in your head every night. {idea}Keep doing what is right, and let the rest go past you.{/idea} Patience is not losing.
old: If I do not answer every jab, I am letting them win.
new: My job is to keep following the truth. Turning aside can be strength.
try: Delete one reply you were going to send to someone who mocked you. Pray instead.

title: You are not their guard, and not their manager.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ freed from carrying other people's choices
then: The Prophet ﷺ longed for his people to believe. Allah reminds him that {idea}if He had willed, they would not have joined partners{/idea}, and there is wisdom in it. {reward}You are not a watcher over them or in charge of their affairs.{/reward} His only duty was to convey.
now: Your brother stopped praying. Your friend is making choices you hate. You carry it like it is your fault. {idea}You can advise, pray, and love.{/idea} {reward}You were never asked to be their guard.{/reward}
old: If the people I love go wrong, I have failed.
new: I convey with love. Their hearts are in Allah's hands, not mine.
try: Make dua by name for one person you worry about, then hand the worry over to Allah.

title: Do not insult their gods, or they will insult Allah.
subtitle: Giving up a small gain to avoid a bigger harm
then: Ibn Abbas reported the idolaters saying: {trap}stop insulting our gods, or we will insult your Lord.{/trap} Qatadah said Muslims had been insulting the idols and the others hit back by insulting Allah. So {idea}Allah forbade it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir ties it to the hadith about the man who curses his own parents by cursing someone else's.
now: A heated comment thread about religion. You type the cutting line about their beliefs. {trap}The reply will drag the name of Allah through the mud.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the most loyal thing you can do is not post it.{/idea}
old: Mocking what others worship is just standing up for the truth.
new: Insulting their gods only invites insults to Allah. Restraint protects what I love.
try: Before posting about someone else's faith today, ask: what reply will this provoke?

title: They swore they would believe if a miracle came.
subtitle: Demanding signs out of defiance, not to find guidance
then: The idolaters of Makkah swore their strongest oaths: {trap}send us a sign and we will surely believe.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they asked out of defiance, not a wish for guidance. The Prophet ﷺ is told to say {idea}signs are only with Allah{/idea}, and the believers are asked how they can be sure the deniers would believe even then.
now: "If I get this job, I will start praying." "If my test comes back clear, I will change." {trap}You set conditions on Allah.{/trap} {idea}The signs you need are mostly already here.{/idea} The deal is a way to delay.
old: I will commit once Allah gives me a clear sign.
new: Waiting for a sign is often a way of not starting. Start now.
try: Find one if-then promise you made to Allah. Do the then part today, without the if.

title: Refuse the first time, and the heart keeps turning away.
subtitle: Rejection hardens into wandering
then: Ibn Abbas said that when they rejected what Allah sent down, {trap}their hearts no longer settled on anything{/trap} and turned away from every good. Mujahid said it means they were kept from faith, as they refused it the first time. {trap}They are left wandering blindly{/trap} in their misguidance.
now: The first time you skip Fajr, it stings. By the tenth time, you barely notice. {trap}Each no makes the next one easier.{/trap} {idea}Answer the call while it still stings.{/idea}
old: I can keep saying not now, and come back whenever I like.
new: Each time I turn away, my heart turns a little more. The first yes matters.
try: Think of one reminder you keep brushing off. Say yes to it once today, even in a small way.

title: Angels, talking dead, the whole world as witness: still no.
subtitle: Guidance is with Allah, not in the size of the miracle
then: The deniers had asked to see angels, or Allah Himself, face to face. The verse answers: even if {idea}angels came, the dead spoke, and every nation stood up to testify{/idea}, they would not believe unless Allah willed. Ibn Kathir says this is because {reward}guidance is with Allah, not with them.{/reward}
now: You think one more lecture, one more book, one perfect argument will finally fix your doubts or your brother's. {idea}Arguments help, but hearts are opened by Allah.{/idea} Ask Him for it directly.
old: If I just find the perfect argument, belief will follow.
new: Guidance is a gift from Allah. I seek it, and I ask Him for it.
try: Make the dua Allahumma ihdini, O Allah guide me, once with full attention today.

title: Every prophet had enemies who whispered pretty words.
subtitle: Devils of humans and jinn, and their decorated speech
then: Allah comforts the Prophet ﷺ: as you have enemies, {idea}every prophet before you had them too.{/idea} Waraqah bin Nawfal had told him no one ever brought this message without being opposed. Qatadah said there are {trap}devils among jinn and among humans who feed each other polished speech{/trap}. The verse calls for patience and trust in Allah.
now: A video with perfect editing, calm music, and a confident voice tells you everything you believe is a joke. {trap}Polished does not mean true.{/trap} {idea}Notice how good it sounds, and then ask what it is actually saying.{/idea}
old: If it sounds smooth and confident, it is probably right.
new: Decorated words are an old trick. I judge the message, not the packaging.
try: Next time a slick clip shakes you, write its main claim in one plain sentence and check it.

title: Hearts that forget the Hereafter lean into the glitter.
subtitle: Who listens to decorated lies, and why
then: Ibn Abbas explained the word as {trap}inclining toward it.{/trap} The polished words find a home in hearts that do not believe in the Hereafter. They like it, settle into it, and then {trap}do what they do{/trap}. As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said it means: let them do whatever they will do.
now: When you have stopped thinking about the next life for a while, the ads hit harder. The influencer life looks better. The shortcut seems fine. {idea}Thinking about the Hereafter is what keeps the glitter from pulling you in.{/idea}
old: I am smart enough not to be fooled by empty talk.
new: It is the forgetful heart that leans toward lies. Remembering the Hereafter protects me.
try: Spend two minutes today thinking honestly about your own death and what you want to have done.

title: Why look for any judge other than Allah?
subtitle: The Book is detailed, and the decision is His

key.label: Where I go for the final word

then: The idolaters argued with the Prophet ﷺ and wanted their own standards to decide. He is told to say: {idea}shall I seek a judge other than Allah{/idea}, when He sent down the Book explained in detail? Ibn Kathir notes that people of earlier scripture {reward}knew it came from Allah in truth{/reward}, because their prophets had foretold him.
now: You disagree with your spouse and both of you start quoting podcasts, uncles, and online threads. {trap}Everyone is shopping for the judge who will side with them.{/trap} {idea}Start by asking what Allah actually said about it.{/idea}
old: I will keep asking around until someone tells me I am right.
new: Allah is the judge, and His Book is clear. I start there.
try: In your next disagreement, look up what the Quran says on the topic before arguing further.

title: His word is complete: true in news, just in command.
subtitle: No one can change what Allah has said
then: Qatadah explained it: {idea}true in what He stated, just in what He decided.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds that everything Allah forbids brings harm, and {reward}none can turn back His judgment{/reward} in this life or the next. He hears what His servants say and knows what they do.
now: News apps update every ten minutes. Last year's advice is this year's mistake. Your boss rewrites the policy again. {reward}Allah's word does not get patched.{/reward} {idea}It was complete before you were born.{/idea}
old: Everything changes, so nothing can be relied on for good.
new: Allah's word is complete and true, and no one can change it.
try: Memorize this one short verse today and repeat it when the world feels unstable.

title: Follow the majority and they will lead you astray.
subtitle: Most people run on guesswork
then: In Makkah the believers were a small group surrounded by a large majority with old customs. Allah tells them {trap}if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says they follow {trap}nothing but conjecture and wishful thinking{/trap}, and doubt their own way.
now: Everyone at work rounds up their timesheets. Everyone in the family takes the loan. Everyone at the party drinks. {idea}A lot of people doing something is not proof.{/idea} It is just a lot of people.
old: If most people do it, it cannot be that wrong.
new: The majority often runs on guesses. I follow what Allah made clear.
try: Pick one thing you do only because everyone does it. Ask honestly if Allah would approve.

title: Your Lord knows best who strays and who is guided.
subtitle: Leave the final sorting to Him

row.title: follow, and leave it to Him

then: Right after warning against following the guessing majority, Allah adds that {idea}He knows best who goes astray and who is guided.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says each one is made easy for what they were created for. The believers did not need to sort the people of Makkah themselves.
now: You see someone without hijab at the mosque, or a bearded man cutting in line, and your mind ranks them instantly. {trap}You have no access to their heart.{/trap} {idea}Allah knows who is guided. Your job is your own path.{/idea}
old: I can tell who is really guided by how they look.
new: Only my Lord knows who is truly guided. I focus on my own way.
try: Catch yourself judging someone's faith today. Replace the thought with a short dua for them.

title: Eat what Allah's name was spoken over.
subtitle: Food tied back to the One who provides it
then: Ibn Kathir says the pagans of Quraysh would eat {trap}what was sacrificed to idols{/trap}. Allah gives the believers permission to {idea}eat what His name was mentioned over{/idea}, tying their food back to Him. The verse links it to faith: if you believe in His signs.
now: Lunch at your desk, eyes on a screen, fork moving on autopilot. You do not even taste it. {idea}Saying Bismillah turns a meal back into a gift{/idea} from someone who chose to feed you today.
old: Eating is just something I do, it has nothing to do with Allah.
new: My food is His provision, and His name over it reminds me who gave it.
try: Say Bismillah out loud before every meal today, and pause one breath before the first bite.

title: He already told you what is forbidden. Why hold back the rest?
subtitle: Clear limits, mercy in need, and desires posing as knowledge
then: Some held back from food Allah had allowed while eating what He had forbidden, following pagan ideas. Allah says {idea}He has already explained in detail what is forbidden{/idea}, with room for real necessity. Then the warning: {trap}many lead others astray by their own desires, without knowledge.{/trap}
now: A relative insists something is haram because it feels wrong to them. Another declares something fine because they want it. {trap}Both are making rules from feelings.{/trap} {idea}Allah already made His limits clear. Learn them instead of guessing.{/idea}
old: What feels right or wrong to me is basically the same as what Allah wants.
new: Allah has explained His limits. My desires do not get to write new ones.
try: Think of one rule you follow or reject on feeling alone. Ask a qualified teacher about it this week.

title: Leave sin on the outside and sin on the inside.
subtitle: Public wrongs and hidden ones are both left behind
then: Mujahid and Qatadah said this covers {trap}all sins, public and secret, few or many.{/trap} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith of An-Nawwas: {idea}sin is what wavers in your chest and you hate for people to find out.{/idea} Every sin, seen or unseen, will be recompensed.
now: In public you are polite and careful. In your private browser history, or in the resentment you nurse quietly, it is a different story. {idea}The test is simple: would you be okay if this were seen?{/idea}
old: As long as my public life is clean, the rest is between me and nobody.
new: Allah asks me to leave the sins people see and the ones they never will.
try: Pick one hidden habit that makes your chest uneasy. Cut it back for just today.

title: Obeying others over Allah is a quiet kind of shirk.
subtitle: Devils feed arguments to their allies
then: Ibn Abbas and As-Suddi reported the idolaters' argument: {trap}you eat what you slaughter but not what Allah causes to die?{/trap} The verse says devils feed such arguments to their allies. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}preferring anyone's word over Allah's law is shirk{/trap}, citing the hadith of Adi bin Hatim about obeying rabbis and monks.
now: A smart-sounding voice online twists a rule into a joke, and suddenly you feel silly following it. {trap}The argument is designed to sound clever.{/trap} {idea}The question is whose word you will follow.{/idea}
old: Shirk means worshipping statues. Following someone's opinion is just being open-minded.
new: When I put anyone's word above Allah's command, I give them a place that is His.
try: Notice one opinion you follow over a clear teaching. Ask yourself why it has that authority.

title: Once dead, then given life and a light to walk with.
subtitle: The believer who walks lit, and the one stuck in the dark
then: Ibn Kathir calls this a parable of the believer who was {trap}dead in confusion and misguidance{/trap}. Allah {reward}gave his heart life with faith{/reward} and a light to walk by among people. Ibn Abbas said the light is the Quran, As-Suddi said Islam. The other stays in layers of darkness he cannot leave.
now: You remember who you were before you started praying for real. Numb, scrolling, angry. {reward}Now there is a light you carry into the office, the kitchen, the hard conversation.{/reward} Do not forget you were once in the dark.
old: Faith is just one of many ways people choose to live.
new: Faith is the difference between being alive with a light and stuck in the dark.
try: Write one sentence about who you were before faith became real. Thank Allah for the change.

title: The great plotters only end up trapping themselves.
subtitle: Every town has powerful wrongdoers, and their plots turn back

row.title: the plot returns
sub: the good end is for the prophets

then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that the leaders opposing him in Makkah are not new. {trap}Every town had great ones among its wrongdoers who plotted{/trap}, and every prophet faced them. Ibn Kathir notes {reward}the good end was always for the messengers.{/reward} The harm of their plots and of misleading others falls on them.
now: Someone at work spins stories to push you out. It feels like they hold all the cards. {idea}Scheming has a way of collapsing on the schemer{/idea}, and they rarely see it coming. And check yourself too: are you plotting against anyone?
old: People who scheme and manipulate always come out on top.
new: Plots against the truth turn back on the plotter. I stay straight and patient.
try: If you are planning to get back at someone, drop the plan today and leave it to Allah.

title: They wanted to be prophets themselves. Allah knows whom to trust.
subtitle: Envy dressed up as a demand for proof
then: The leaders said they would not believe until {trap}they got what the messengers got.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to their complaint that the Quran should have come to a great man of Makkah or Taif. They belittled the Prophet ﷺ out of envy, though they had called him Al-Amin. {idea}Allah knows best where to place His message.{/idea}
now: A younger colleague gets the promotion. A friend gets the blessing you prayed for. {trap}You start finding faults in them{/trap}, when the real feeling is: why not me? {idea}Allah knows who to trust with what.{/idea}
old: If someone gets what I wanted, they must not deserve it.
new: Allah knows best who to trust with each gift. Envy blinds me to it.
try: Congratulate, sincerely, one person who got something you wanted.

title: An open chest, or one that feels like climbing the sky.
subtitle: How guidance feels from the inside
then: Ibn Abbas said Allah {reward}opens the heart of the one He guides to Tawhid and faith{/reward}, making it easy. For the other, faith feels so heavy it is {trap}like trying to climb into the sky.{/trap} Sa'id bin Jubayr said Islam finds every path in that heart blocked.
now: Some days prayer feels like breathing out. Other days it feels like dragging yourself up a hill with no air. {idea}That feeling is worth noticing.{/idea} {reward}An open chest is something you can ask Allah for.{/reward}
old: If faith feels heavy, that is just how it is for me.
new: An open chest is a gift from Allah, and I can ask Him for it.
try: Say Rabbi ishrah li sadri, my Lord expand my chest, before your next prayer.

title: This is your Lord's path, and it runs straight.
subtitle: The signs laid out for those who take heed
then: After describing those who strayed and blocked others, Allah points to {idea}the path of your Lord, straight{/idea}, meaning Islam revealed through this Quran. Ibn Kathir says the signs are made clear {reward}for people of sound understanding{/reward} who take heed of what Allah and His Messenger convey.
now: Life feels like a maze of choices: which job, which city, which friends. {idea}The main road is not hidden.{/idea} Most of the twists come from looking away from it. The signs are clear to whoever stops and thinks.
old: The right path is confusing and hard to find.
new: My Lord's path is straight and clear when I take the time to reflect.
try: Before one decision today, ask: which choice keeps me on Allah's straight path?

title: At the end of the straight path: a Home of Peace.
subtitle: Paradise with their Lord, and Him as their protector

row.title: a safe path, a safe home

then: Ibn Kathir says Paradise is called {reward}the Home of Peace{/reward} because its people are safe, having walked the straight path of the prophets. {idea}Just as their way was free of wickedness, so is their home.{/idea} Allah is their Wali, their protector and helper, because of what they did.
now: You come home after a brutal day: traffic, an angry client, a sick kid. You just want one place with no stress. {reward}That longing is a small picture of the Home of Peace.{/reward} The road there is built from today's quiet choices.
old: Peace is something I will never really have.
new: A Home of Peace waits at the end of the straight path, and Allah is my protector on it.
try: Do one kind thing today that brings peace to someone else's home.

title: We used each other, they will say. The deal ends badly.
subtitle: Jinn and their human followers gathered on the Day
then: Ibn Jurayj said that before Islam a traveler would arrive in a valley and say: {trap}I seek refuge with the master jinn of this valley.{/trap} Al-Hasan said they benefited from each other: the jinn commanded and the humans obeyed. On the Day, that arrangement is exposed, and {trap}it ends in the Fire{/trap}, except as Allah wills.
now: A friendship built on covering for each other. A business partner who helps you cut corners while you help him. {trap}It feels like mutual benefit.{/trap} {idea}Ask where the arrangement is taking both of you.{/idea}
old: As long as we both get something out of it, the relationship is fine.
new: A partnership in wrong is not a benefit. It is a shared road to loss.
try: Think of one relationship where you enable each other's worst habits. Change your part of it.

title: Wrongdoers end up with wrongdoers as their allies.
subtitle: The company you keep is earned
then: Qatadah said wrongdoers become allies of each other, following one another into the Fire. Ibn Zayd recited {trap}whoever turns from the remembrance of the Merciful, We assign him a devil as companion.{/trap} Ibn Kathir adds that Allah also {trap}sets wrongdoers over one another{/trap}, as a just result.
now: You start lying at work and suddenly your lunch group is the people who lie best. You start gossiping and the gossips find you. {idea}Your deeds shape your circle.{/idea} The good news: it works the other way too.
old: My friends just happened. They have nothing to do with how I live.
new: The company I keep follows the deeds I choose. I can change both.
try: Spend some time this week with one person whose habits you want to grow into.

title: Did messengers not come to you? Yes, we admit it.
subtitle: The world's glitter deceived them, and they confess

row.title: we were distracted
sub: by the glitter of this life

then: On the Day, jinn and humans are asked: {idea}did messengers not come to you, reciting My verses and warning you of this Day?{/idea} They admit it. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they were deceived by the beauty, adornment and desires of this life{/trap}, and wasted their lives rejecting what came.
now: Your phone has a Quran app, a dozen lectures saved, a friend who reminds you. No one can say they were not told. {trap}The danger is not ignorance. It is distraction.{/trap} {idea}You already know enough to act on something.{/idea}
old: I will take faith seriously once I learn more.
new: I have already been reminded. The question is whether the world is distracting me.
try: Act today on one thing you already know you should do, instead of learning something new.

title: No town is destroyed before it is warned.
subtitle: Allah's justice: the message always comes first

row.title: warning first
sub: no one is left without excuse

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah sent messengers and books so that {idea}no one could say they were punished without being told.{/idea} He cites: {reward}We never punish until We have sent a messenger{/reward}, and every nation had a warner. The Makkans were hearing their warning right then.
now: Your manager gives you a written warning before any firing. You still feel it was unfair. {idea}Allah is more just than any manager.{/idea} Every reminder you receive is part of that warning, given out of mercy.
old: Allah might punish me for things I was never told about.
new: Allah always warns before He holds anyone to account. His reminders are mercy.
try: Think of a recent reminder you received. Thank Allah for the warning and respond to it.

title: Everyone gets a level matching what they did.
subtitle: Degrees for each, and nothing missed
then: At-Tabari said everyone who obeys or disobeys has {idea}ranks according to their works{/idea}, good for good and evil for evil. Ibn Jarir adds that all they did, {reward}your Lord was aware of and recorded{/reward}, to repay them when they return to Him.
now: You hold the door for someone. You hold your tongue in an argument. No one claps. {reward}None of it is lost.{/reward} {idea}Each small choice moves you up or down a level{/idea} with a Lord who never looks away.
old: Small good deeds do not really count for much.
new: Every deed builds my level, and my Lord does not miss any of it.
try: Do one small kindness today that no one will see, and leave it with Allah.

title: He needs nothing from you, and He is full of mercy.
subtitle: He could replace you, as you replaced others
then: Ibn Kathir explains Al-Ghani as {idea}free of needing His creatures in any way{/idea}, while they need Him in every situation. He is also {reward}full of mercy{/reward}. If they defy Him, He can bring others in their place, as He raised them from the offspring of earlier people.
now: Some days you pray like you are doing Allah a favor. Then you notice how many generations lived in your house, your street, before you. {idea}He does not need you. He wants good for you.{/idea} That is what mercy looks like.
old: My prayers and good deeds are something Allah needs from me.
new: Allah needs nothing from me. My worship is for my own good, and His mercy surrounds me.
try: Before your next prayer, remind yourself: I am the one who needs this.

title: What you are promised is coming, and no one escapes it.
subtitle: The Resurrection is certain
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say that what they were promised {idea}will surely come{/idea}, meaning the Resurrection. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they cannot escape{/trap}, for Allah is able to bring them back even after they turn to dust and bones.
now: You plan your retirement down to the year. Your holiday is booked months ahead. {idea}The one appointment that is truly certain{/idea} gets the least planning. Give it a slot in your thinking.
old: The Day of Judgment is far away and not worth planning for.
new: It is certainly coming. I can prepare for it like any real appointment.
try: Write down one thing you want to have done before you meet Allah, and take one step on it.

title: Keep doing your thing. I will keep doing mine. Time will tell.
subtitle: A calm challenge from the Prophet ﷺ
then: Ibn Abbas explained the phrase as {idea}your way{/idea}: stay on your way if you think it is right, and I will stay on mine. Ibn Kathir says Allah kept His promise. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ later entered Makkah and his message spread across Arabia{/reward} in his lifetime.
now: Your family thinks your prayer, your modest choices, your refusal of the shady deal are naive. You do not need to win the argument tonight. {idea}Keep working your way, quietly and well.{/idea} The end will show.
old: I have to convince everyone right now that I am right.
new: I can keep doing what is right calmly, and let the end show who was right.
try: The next time someone mocks a good choice of yours, smile, keep going, and say nothing.

title: A share for Allah, a share for the idols, and they cheated.
subtitle: Dividing what Allah created between Him and partners
then: Ibn Abbas described it: they set aside part of their crops for Allah and part for the idol. If anything from Allah's share fell into the idol's, {trap}they kept it there, saying the idol is poor.{/trap} If the idol's share spilled into Allah's, they took it back. {idea}Evil is how they judge.{/idea}
now: You set aside an hour for Quran and an hour for TV. The Quran hour gets eaten by emails. The TV hour never does. {trap}Allah's share always shrinks first.{/trap} Notice which side wins when things collide.
old: I give Allah His share of my time and money. That is enough.
new: Everything I have is His. And when time collides, His share should not be the first to go.
try: Protect one small slot today for Allah that nothing else is allowed to take.

title: Their partners made even killing their children seem right.
subtitle: How fear and custom can disguise a terrible wrong

picture.label: How it was made to look fair

then: Ibn Kathir says the devils {trap}made it seem fair to kill their children for fear of poverty{/trap}, and to bury daughters for fear of dishonor. As-Suddi said it was to destroy them and confuse their religion. {idea}Allah disliked these practices{/idea}, and tells the Prophet ﷺ to leave them with their fabrications.
now: Fear of money, fear of what people say. These still push parents to choices that hurt their kids: never home, always angry, pressure that crushes. {trap}Fear can make something harmful look like responsibility.{/trap} {idea}Look at your children with the eyes of mercy.{/idea}
old: Whatever I do out of fear for my family's future must be right.
new: Fear can make harm look reasonable. I check my choices with Allah's mercy.
try: Spend fifteen minutes today fully with a child in your life, phone away.

title: They made their own forbidden lists and called them Allah's.
subtitle: Invented taboos on cattle and crops
then: Ibn Abbas and others said these were animals they had declared forbidden, like the Bahirah and Wasilah. Qatadah called it {trap}a prohibition the devils set on their wealth, extremism that did not come from Allah.{/trap} They pinned it on Allah's religion. {idea}He never allowed or approved it.{/idea}
now: Someone in your family insists you cannot do something, wear something, say something, "because it is religion." No source, just habit. {trap}Adding rules can be as false as removing them.{/trap} {idea}Ask where it comes from.{/idea}
old: Being stricter than needed is always safer.
new: Inventing rules and calling them Allah's is a lie against Him, even when it looks pious.
try: Pick one strict rule you follow. Find out this week whether it is from Allah or from habit.

title: Good for our men, forbidden to our women, unless it died.
subtitle: Unfair rules women carried in the name of religion
then: Ibn Abbas said this was about milk and newborn animals: {trap}the men got them, the women did not, unless the animal was born dead{/trap}, then they all shared. Allah forbade it. Mujahid and others said He will repay them {idea}for what their tongues falsely described{/idea} as lawful and forbidden.
now: At family gatherings the men eat first and the women get what is left. Someone says it is just how religious families do it. {trap}Unfairness wrapped in religion is still unfairness.{/trap} {idea}Allah is wise and knows what is really being done.{/idea}
old: If it is an old custom, it must be part of the faith.
new: Allah condemned customs that favored men in His name. He sees through the label.
try: At the next family meal, make sure someone who is usually served last gets served first.

title: They lost: their children, their provision, and the truth.
subtitle: Foolishness without knowledge, and what it cost
then: Ibn Abbas said: {trap}if you want to know how ignorant the Arabs were, recite the verses after one hundred and thirty in Al-An'am.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they lost this life by harming their children and restricting their own wealth, and the next by {trap}lying about Allah.{/trap}
now: You make big decisions on rumors, a cousin's advice, a viral post. Then you defend them as if Allah commanded them. {idea}Foolishness is acting without knowledge.{/idea} Learning first protects your family and your faith.
old: I know enough to make religious decisions for my family on my own.
new: Acting on religion without knowledge cost people everything. I learn before I decide.
try: Before your next big family decision, ask someone knowledgeable and trustworthy first.

title: Eat from the harvest, give its due, and do not waste.
subtitle: Gardens, palms and olives, with three instructions

row.title: His, with a share for others

then: The idolaters had carved up crops and cattle with invented rules. Allah reminds them {idea}He produced the gardens, trellised and wild.{/idea} Mujahid said when the poor are present on harvest day, {reward}give them some of it.{/reward} Ibn Kathir reads the warning on excess as mainly about eating, citing: eat and drink without extravagance or arrogance.
now: Payday lands. The first thought is the new phone, the takeaway, the upgrade. {reward}This verse puts someone else's share right next to yours{/reward}, on the same day the money arrives. {trap}And it warns against eating and spending past what you need.{/trap}
old: What I earned is mine to enjoy however I like.
new: It came from Allah. I enjoy it, share some, and do not overdo it.
try: On your next payday, give a small amount to someone in need the same day.

title: Animals to carry and feed you. Eat, and skip Satan's footsteps.
subtitle: Provision received with gratitude, not invented rules
then: Ibn Zayd explained it: some animals carry people and loads, others are {reward}eaten and milked, with their wool used for mats and clothes.{/reward} All are Allah's provision. The pagans had followed devilish ideas in forbidding some of them. {trap}Do not follow Satan's footsteps; he is a clear enemy.{/trap}
now: Your wool jumper, your morning milk, the leather of your shoes. {reward}All of it came from animals Allah made useful to you.{/reward} {trap}Satan rarely asks for a leap. He asks for one small step at a time.{/trap}
old: Satan only matters when I am tempted by something huge.
new: Satan works in footsteps. I watch the small steps, and I thank Allah for what He gave.
try: Look at one thing you use today that came from an animal, and thank Allah for it by name.

title: Male or female, or what is in the womb? Show your proof.
subtitle: Sheep and goats, and a question about invented bans
then: Ibn Kathir says these verses expose the ignorance of the Arabs before Islam, who banned certain animals. Ibn Abbas explained: {idea}Allah did not forbid any of these.{/idea} Does a womb give anything but males and females? So why ban some and allow others? {trap}Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful.{/trap}
now: Someone tells you a thing is forbidden. You ask where it says so, and they get offended. {idea}Asking for knowledge is not rudeness. The Quran itself asks it.{/idea} Ask politely, and keep asking.
old: Questioning a religious claim is disrespectful.
new: The Quran itself asks for proof. I can ask, kindly, where a rule comes from.
try: Next time you hear a surprising religious claim, ask gently: what is the source?

title: Were you there when Allah gave this command?
subtitle: Camels and cattle, and lies told to mislead
then: The same question repeats for camels and cattle. Then a sharper one: {idea}were you present when Allah ordered this?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it mocks their invented bans. {trap}No one is more unjust than one who lies about Allah to mislead people without knowledge.{/trap} He names Amr bin Luhay as the first to change the religion this way.
now: You forward a message: "The Prophet ﷺ said..." You never checked it. Hundreds of people now believe it. {trap}One unchecked claim can mislead many.{/trap} {idea}Were you there? Do you know?{/idea}
old: Sharing a religious message is always good, even if I am not sure it is true.
new: Spreading claims about Allah without knowledge can mislead people. I check first.
try: Before forwarding any religious message today, check its source or do not send it.

title: The list of forbidden food is short, and mercy covers need.
subtitle: What revelation actually names, against invented bans
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to answer those who invented bans: {idea}I do not find in what was revealed to me{/idea} anything forbidden except these. Ibn Kathir notes other texts add to this list. Ibn Abbas said: {reward}what Allah allowed is lawful, what He forbade is unlawful, and there is no sin in what He did not mention.{/reward}
now: Some people make religion feel like a minefield, where every step might be wrong. {idea}Allah's limits are clear and few compared to the open land.{/idea} {reward}And when you are truly forced, His mercy is there.{/reward}
old: Religion is mostly a long list of things I cannot do.
new: Allah's limits are clear and few, and His mercy is wide.
try: Make a note of five good things Allah has made fully allowed for you, and enjoy one today with thanks.

title: Some restrictions came as the price of rebellion.
subtitle: Extra limits earned by defiance, and the loophole trick
then: Allah tells of foods He forbade to the Children of Israel, and says {trap}this was a recompense for their rebellion{/trap}, not a rule they took from Ya'qub as they claimed. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith warning against those who, when fats were forbidden, {trap}melted them down, sold them, and used the price.{/trap}
now: You would never take a bribe. But a "gift" after the contract? You would never cheat a customer. But the small print? {trap}Renaming a thing to slip past a limit is the oldest trick.{/trap} {idea}Respect what the rule is for.{/idea}
old: If I find a technical way around a rule, I am not doing anything wrong.
new: Getting around Allah's limits with tricks is its own kind of rebellion.
try: Think of one place you use a technicality to get around something. Drop the trick this week.

title: If they deny you, say: your Lord's mercy is vast.
subtitle: Hope and warning in the same breath
then: Even when the Prophet ﷺ is rejected, his reply opens with {reward}your Lord is the Owner of vast mercy{/reward}, an invitation. Then the warning that His punishment is not turned away from criminals. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}Allah often joins hope and warning{/idea}, as at the end of this same surah.
now: You have messed up badly, again. Part of you says it is over. {reward}The first thing this verse says, even to those rejecting the Prophet ﷺ, is that mercy is vast.{/reward} {idea}The warning is real. So is the open door.{/idea}
old: After what I have done, there is only punishment waiting for me.
new: His mercy is vast and open to me. The warning is there so I walk through that door.
try: Make istighfar today for the one thing you think is too big to be forgiven.

title: If Allah wanted, we would not have done it, they said.
subtitle: Blaming fate for your own choices

row.title: it happened, so it is fine

then: The idolaters argued: {trap}if Allah had willed, we and our fathers would not have done shirk{/trap}, so He must approve. Ibn Kathir says earlier nations used the same excuse. If it were true, He would not have punished them. {idea}Do you have any knowledge? You only follow guesses.{/idea}
now: "It was written for me." You say it about the lie, the shortcut, the habit you keep feeding. {trap}Decree becomes a blanket you hide under.{/trap} {idea}Allah's knowledge of your choice does not make the choice His.{/idea}
old: If I did it, Allah must have wanted it, so I am off the hook.
new: Allah knowing what I will do does not make wrong right. I still own my choices.
try: Catch one moment today where you blame fate. Replace it with: I chose this, and I can choose again.

title: The final argument belongs to Allah.
subtitle: He could have guided all of you
then: After their excuse about fate, the reply: {idea}with Allah is the perfect, far-reaching argument.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says He has the perfect wisdom to guide or misguide whom He wills, and is pleased with the believers. Ad-Dahhak said: {trap}no one has an excuse if he disobeys Allah.{/trap}
now: You have rehearsed your excuse for years. Busy, stressed, raised that way, nobody taught me. {idea}Picture saying it to the One who knows every hour you had.{/idea} Better to drop the excuse now and just ask for help.
old: I have good reasons for not changing, and Allah will accept them.
new: Allah's proof is complete. Instead of excuses, I can ask Him for guidance.
try: Write your favorite excuse down, then cross it out and write a dua for help instead.

title: Bring your witnesses. If they lie, do not testify with them.
subtitle: Refusing to join a false testimony
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask them to {idea}bring witnesses that Allah forbade this.{/idea} If they testify anyway, Ibn Kathir says {trap}their testimony is false{/trap}, so do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who deny the signs and set up equals to their Lord.
now: The whole family agrees a relative is to blame. Everyone in the meeting nods along to a claim you know is wrong. {trap}It is easy to add your nod.{/trap} {idea}You can stay silent, or say what you know, but do not sign off on a lie.{/idea}
old: If everyone else is saying it, it is fine for me to agree.
new: When a group backs something false, I do not add my voice to it.
try: In the next group conversation where something unfair is said, decline to agree, even quietly.

title: Come, hear what your Lord truly forbade.
subtitle: The first of the commands Ibn Mas'ud called a sealed will
then: After all the invented food bans, the Prophet ﷺ says: {idea}come, I will recite what your Lord actually forbade.{/idea} Ibn Mas'ud said whoever wants to read the will of the Messenger ﷺ on which he placed his seal should read these verses. Ibn Kathir notes {reward}kindness to parents{/reward} sits right next to worshipping Allah alone.
now: You argue about small details of religion online while not calling your mother back for a week. {idea}These verses are the real list.{/idea} {reward}Your parents are near the top, right after Allah.{/reward}
old: Being religious is mostly about the small details I argue about.
new: Allah's real list starts with Him alone, kindness to parents, and protecting life.
try: Call or visit one of your parents today, or make dua for them if they have passed.

title: Fair measure, honest words, even against your own family.
subtitle: Orphans, weights, testimony and promises
then: Ibn Abbas said that when this was revealed, guardians of orphans became so careful they kept the orphans' food separate. Allah then eased it. Ibn Kathir says {idea}justice is commanded in actions and words, with near and far relatives alike.{/idea} And {reward}no one is burdened beyond what they can bear{/reward}; an honest mistake after real effort is not a sin.
now: Your brother is in the wrong in the family dispute, and everyone looks at you. {idea}Being fair now costs something.{/idea} The same with the bill you split, the hours you log, the promise you made. {reward}Allah asks only what you can carry.{/reward}
old: I am fair, except when it is my own family.
new: Justice counts most when it is against my own people. And Allah asks only what I can bear.
try: In one small matter today, choose the fair option even if it costs you or someone close.

title: One straight path, and many side roads that scatter you.
subtitle: The line drawn in the sand
then: Ibn Mas'ud reported the Prophet ﷺ {idea}drew a straight line in the sand and said: this is Allah's path.{/idea} Then he drew lines to its right and left: {trap}on each of these paths is a devil calling to it.{/trap} Then he recited this verse. Ibn Kathir notes the path is singular because truth is one, and the other ways are many.
now: A new guru every month. A new trend every week. Each one shouts from its own side road. {trap}You end up scattered, pulled in every direction.{/trap} {idea}Hold the one line, and the noise from the sides gets easier to ignore.{/idea}
old: Trying every path is how I will find the right one.
new: There is one straight path, and the side roads exist to pull me off it.
try: Draw a straight line on paper with lines branching off. Name one side road you want to stop walking.

title: Musa was given a complete Book, as a reward for doing good.
subtitle: The Tawrah: detail, guidance, mercy
then: Right after the straight path, Allah praises the Tawrah. Ibn Kathir notes {idea}Allah often mentions the Quran and the Tawrah together.{/idea} The Book was complete for Musa's law and given {reward}as a reward for his doing right and obeying{/reward}, citing: is the reward for good anything but good?
now: You worked carefully, honestly, kept your promises, and then a door opened. {reward}That is often how Allah works: good answered with more good.{/reward} {idea}Keep doing your best quietly. It is being noticed.{/idea}
old: Doing good rarely gets me anywhere.
new: Allah answers good with good. The gift often follows the effort.
try: Do one task today with full care and excellence, even if no one checks it.

title: This Book is blessed. Follow it, and mercy follows you.
subtitle: The Quran as Allah's firm rope
then: After the Tawrah, the Quran: {reward}a blessed Book, so follow it and be mindful of Allah, that you may receive mercy.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says Allah tells His servants to {idea}understand it, hold to it, and call others to it{/idea}, because it is the firm rope of Allah, blessed for whoever acts on it.
now: There is a beautiful mushaf in your house, wrapped in cloth on a high shelf. It gets dusted more than it gets opened. {idea}The blessing is in following it, not keeping it safe.{/idea}
old: Having the Quran in my home brings blessing on its own.
new: The Quran's blessing reaches me when I read it and follow it.
try: Take the Quran down today and read one page, then pick one line to act on.

title: No more saying: the Book was not sent to us.
subtitle: The Quran removes the excuse of not knowing

row.title: it is not in my language

then: Ibn Abbas said the two groups were the Jews and Christians. Ibn Jarir explained the Quran came so the Arabs could not say: {trap}we did not understand their books, it was not our language, we were busy and unaware.{/trap} {idea}Now a Book had come to them in their own tongue.{/idea}
now: "I do not understand Arabic." "I never had a teacher." Yet translations sit in your phone in your language, with audio, for free. {idea}The excuse of distance is gone.{/idea} The Book was sent to you too.
old: I cannot really understand the Quran, so it is not for me.
new: The Quran was sent so no one could say it never reached them. It reached me.
try: Open a translation in your own language and read five verses with full attention.

title: We would be better guided, they said. Now proof came.
subtitle: The boast answered by a clear sign

row.title: if only we had a Book
I have it now
sub: what am I doing with it?

then: The Arabs had sworn that if a warner came they would be {trap}more guided than any nation.{/trap} The reply: {reward}a clear proof, guidance and mercy have come to you.{/reward} As-Suddi explained the word for turning away as hindering others from it; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said it means turning away.
now: "If I lived near a great mosque I would go every day." "If I had more time I would learn." {trap}The if-only version of you is always better.{/trap} {idea}The real test is what you do with what you already have.{/idea}
old: If I had better circumstances, I would be much more devoted.
new: Guidance is already in my hands. The question is what I do with it now.
try: Pick one if-only you often say. Do a small version of it today with what you have.

title: When certain signs arrive, late faith no longer helps.
subtitle: Waiting until it is too late to turn
then: The deniers kept delaying, as if waiting for angels or for Allah to come. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith in Bukhari: {trap}the Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west; when people see it, all will believe, but then faith will not help one who did not believe before.{/trap} {idea}Faith and good deeds must come before that.{/idea}
now: "I will get serious after the wedding." "After the kids are older." "When I retire." {trap}Every delay assumes the door stays open.{/trap} {idea}Today it is open.{/idea}
old: I will turn to Allah properly once life settles down.
new: There is a point where turning back stops counting. Today is not that day.
try: Make sincere tawbah today for one thing you have been saving for later.

title: Those who split their religion into camps: you are not of them.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ kept clear of division
then: Several early scholars said this was about earlier communities who split into sects. Ibn Kathir says it {idea}applies to all who divide the religion{/idea} into camps of opinion and desire, since the law Allah sent is one. He cites the hadith: {reward}we prophets are brothers, and our religion is one.{/reward} Their matter is left to Allah.
now: Two mosques in the same town that do not greet each other. A group chat that turns every topic into a fight between labels. {trap}You start loving your camp more than your Lord.{/trap} {idea}Hold the path, and leave the scoring of others to Allah.{/idea}
old: Defending my group against other Muslims is defending the religion.
new: Splitting the religion into camps is something the Prophet ﷺ stood apart from.
try: Greet or thank someone this week from a Muslim group you usually avoid.

title: One good deed counts ten. One bad deed counts one.
subtitle: How generously Allah keeps the record

row.title: a good intention is written
sub: and a sin left for Allah too

then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith from Ibn Abbas: {reward}whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, it is written as one good deed; if he does it, ten up to seven hundred and more.{/reward} Whoever intends a sin and leaves it for Allah's sake, that too is written as good. {idea}If he does it, one sin, unless Allah erases it.{/idea}
now: You meant to visit your sick aunt but the day ran out. You were about to send the angry text, then deleted it. {reward}Both were noticed and written.{/reward} {idea}Allah keeps your record more generously than you keep your own.{/idea}
old: My bad deeds outweigh everything good I try to do.
new: Allah multiplies my good and counts my bad only once. Even my intentions count.
try: Intend three good deeds this morning. Do at least one before sunset.

title: My Lord guided me: the upright way of Ibrahim.
subtitle: A firm religion, easy and pure
then: After all the arguments with the idolaters, the Prophet ﷺ is told to declare: {idea}my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a firm religion, the way of Ibrahim, upright.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites Ibn Abbas: the Prophet ﷺ was asked which religion Allah loves most, and said {reward}the upright, easy way.{/reward}
now: Someone tells you faith is a burden that makes life heavy. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ described it as upright and easy.{/reward} {idea}Ibrahim's way was simple: turn to Allah alone and walk straight.{/idea}
old: Being religious means making life harder for myself.
new: The way of Ibrahim is upright and easy: Allah alone, and a straight walk.
try: Say today, from the heart: my Lord has guided me. Thank Him for it once.

title: My prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death: all for Allah.
subtitle: One sentence that covers everything
then: The idolaters prayed to idols and sacrificed to them. The Prophet ﷺ is told to declare the opposite: {idea}my prayer and my rites are for Allah alone.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says Allah commanded him to {reward}dedicate his intention and heart sincerely to Him.{/reward} Then the circle widens to his whole life and death.
now: You pray at 1 p.m. and then walk back into a meeting as if Allah stayed on the mat. {idea}This verse puts the commute, the work, the dinner table, and the last breath in the same sentence as prayer.{/idea}
old: My religious life and my normal life are two separate things.
new: My prayer, my work, my whole life and my death can all be for Allah.
try: Before you start work today, quietly say this verse's meaning: this too is for You.

title: He has no partner. I was commanded this, and I submit first.
subtitle: The one who calls is the first to obey
then: Qatadah said {idea}first of the Muslims means the first of this ummah{/idea}, since all prophets before called to Islam. Ibn Kathir lists Nuh, Ibrahim, Yusuf, Musa and the disciples of Isa, each saying they were Muslims, meaning {reward}they submitted to Allah alone.{/reward}
now: You tell your kids to put their phones down at dinner while yours is in your hand. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ was the first to do what he called others to.{/idea} The one who calls goes first.
old: It is enough to tell others what is right.
new: The Prophet ﷺ was first to submit. I start with myself before I tell others.
try: Pick one piece of advice you give others often. Do it yourself today first.

title: No one carries another's load. Each soul earns for itself.
subtitle: Why look for any other lord?
then: The Prophet ﷺ asks: {idea}shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is Lord of all things?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says this verse is about trusting Him, after the last one was about worshipping Him, like "You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help." Then: {reward}no soul carries another's burden{/reward}, a sign of His perfect justice.
now: You grew up hearing your family's mistakes would follow you. Or you secretly hope your parents' prayers will cover your own neglect. {reward}Neither is true.{/reward} {idea}You are not your father's sins, and you are not saved by your mother's tahajjud.{/idea}
old: I am stuck with what my family did, or covered by what they did.
new: I carry my own deeds. That is fair, and it means my path is mine to walk.
try: Put down one guilt that belongs to someone else, and pick up one good deed that is yours.

title: Placed on earth, ranked differently, and tested in what you were given.
subtitle: The surah closes with warning and mercy together
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah made people differ in {idea}provision, character, looks and color{/idea} to test them: the rich in how they thank, the poor in how they are patient. The surah ends: swift in penalty, and {reward}Forgiving, Merciful.{/reward} He closes with the hadith: {reward}My mercy overcomes My anger.{/reward}
now: Your colleague earns double. Your neighbor's kids got into the good school. You compare all day. {idea}Their portion is their test. Yours is yours.{/idea} {reward}And the One running the test has mercy that outweighs His anger.{/reward}
old: What I have compared to others shows what I am worth.
new: What I was given is my test, not my score. And His mercy is greater than His anger.
try: Name one thing you have more of than others and one you have less of. Thank Allah for the first, and be patient with the second.
